title: Ramayana trailer takes China by storm, viewers call it better than Hollywood, Chinese films: 'We can't make such epics'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nitesh Tiwari’s soon-to-release Ramayana has been billed as the most expensive Indian movie ever made. On a scale so grand that it evokes Hollywood blockbusters, Ramayana has global aspirations, including a wide rollout in China. So far, it has managed to raise intrigue with its teaser and trailer. The Ramayana trailer , in particular, has been huge in China, crossing a million views in just a few hours. The comments, thousands of them, are largely praising the movie’s scale, calling it even better than homegrown Chinese films.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama in the movie. Chinese viewers go ga-ga over Ramayana Comments on the Ramayana trailer posted in China ranged from surprise over an Indian movie delivering this scale to disappointment over Chinese films not matching up. One person compared Ramayana to the Fengshen movie series, saying, “The special effects are much better than Fengshen,” and wrote that Ramayana is better than the $360-million smash hit. Another wondered if these effects could have elevated the series. “Is this effect what domestic directors wanted for Investiture of the Gods?” Another comment read, “How does this feel better than the domestic films from the past two years?”

Meanwhile, Many Chinese viewers bemoaned that local filmmakers are unable to give Chinese mythology the same treatment. “We can't make such epic myths because these sh***y directors lack respect for our national myths, complained one.

Notably, Many other comments called the movie’s effects better than even some Hollywood blockbusters. “The filming is better than Legendary,” read one comment, referring to Legendary Entertainment, which has produced films like 300, Clash of the Titans, Godzilla, and the Jurassic World franchise. Legendary is best known for mounting its monsterverse featuring King Kong and Godzilla. Another comment called Ramayana “India's own Odyssey.”

As per the latest buzz, Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama in Ramayana, directed by Nitesh Tiwari. The two-part movie also stars Yash as Ravana and Sai Pallavi as Sita. Yash is also the movie’s co-producer, partnering with Namit Malhotra. The movie also features a large ensemble cast, including Ravie Dubey, Sunny Deol, Arun Govil, Lara Dutta, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, and Kunal Kapoor. Ramayana Part One is slated to rollout worldwide on November 6, ahead of Diwali. The movie's global distribution is being handled by Sony Pictures. As part of the deal, in China, Ramayana will be distributed by Sony under the local title Ramayana: The Legend of the Prince.

title: Students detained ahead of Amit Shah's Alwar visit as they planned protest to demand his resignation over CJP crackdown
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Rajasthan Police detained a group of college students in Alwar on Sunday ahead of Union home minister Amit Shah's public programme in the city as they were planning to hold a protest and show black flags to him.

Adding to this, There's been a sustained Opposition demand for Union home minister Amit Shah's resignation over the police action against student protesters in the national capital in July. (PTI Photo) Shah , accompanied by Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma , is scheduled to address a public meeting at Vijay Nagar Ground in Alwar and launch development projects worth ₹ 6,279 crore rupees across the state, including ₹ 783 crore rupees worth of projects in Alwar district.

Meanwhile, The protesters had planned to raise the issue of the lathi-charge on students at Jantar Mantar in Delhi during the Cockroach Janta Party protest in July. Other issues on their list were the poor condition of roads, the alleged Matsya scam (corruption in the fisheries department) and the demand for restoration of student union elections in Rajasthan, the sources further told PTI.

Notably, The Alwar detentions come against the backdrop of a wider pattern of preventive detentions ahead of Shah's public engagements in recent weeks, as well as a sustained Opposition demand for the home minister's resignation over the police action against student protesters in the national capital in July.

As per the latest buzz, In Pune on August 1, several office-bearers of the Maharashtra Youth Congress and Pune City Congress were taken into custody shortly after midnight ahead of Shah and National Security Advisor Ajit Doval's visit to the city. The Youth Congress alleged its leaders were held for nearly 16 hours and that police seized their mobile phones during the detention.

In further updates, Separately in Pune the same day, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Vasant More was detained after announcing he would stage a protest during Shah's visit. Police shared the detention was preventive and not linked to any criminal case, and was carried out to avoid disruption to the visit and an award ceremony for Doval.

On top of that, The July 20 police action cited by the Alwar protesters relates to the student-led protest movement at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak, which had drawn activists under banners including the All India Students Association and the Cockroach Janta Party.
Those protests led to the resignation of senior BJP leader Dharmendra Pradhanas education minister in PM Narendra Modi's government.

title: Yash clarifies the ₹4000 crore budget for Ramayana, says it runs on Hollywood math: 'Revenue is global too'
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s soon-to-release Ramayana has been billed as the most expensive Indian movie ever made. Its producer, Namit Malhotra , had famously claimed that the two-part movie has a budget of $500 million, or ₹ 4000 crore rupees. This figure has invited both awe and ridicule, with many trade insiders fearing the movie would not break even. But the movie’s star and co-producer, Yash , has now clarified what the budget means, and why the makers are not too worried about the box-office prospects.

Adding to this, Yash plays Ravana in the new adaptation of the Ramayana. Yash on Ramayana budget In his recent appearance on Aap Ki Adalat, Yash was asked by host Rajat Sharma how the movie’s scale differs from what the star has done so far, citing the ₹ 4000-crore rupees budget. Yash clarified that the ₹ 4000 crore rupees is not the budget for Ramayana Part One and also explained the ‘Hollywood math’ behind it. He shared, “That is a misconception, so let me clarify it to everyone. ₹ 4000 crore rupees is the budget for the two-part movie, including rollout and promotion. It is the same as Hollywood. Our partner (Namit) shared this after including all that. Wahan ka maths waisa hi hota hai (The math there is like this). A budget equal to the movie, or sometimes more, they spend on promotion because it is global. But the revenue is global too.”

Meanwhile, Yash shared it was essential to spend that much money to take Indian cinema global, adding that if India doesn’t, other movie industries will take that advantage. “Cinema is a soft power. All of us have to work really hard towards it. Whatever happens, we will work hard and do our job properly. If not today, then tomorrow we’ll make it happen. If we don’t, someone else will -, but it should happen. That is what I feel. Both Ramayana and Toxic are attempts to position Indian cinema as global films,” he added.

Notably, Yash plays the antagonist Ravana in the two Ramayana films, with Ranbir Kapoor playing Lord Rama and Sai Pallavi playing Sita. He is also the movie’s co-producer, partnering with Namit Malhotra. The movie, directed by Nitesh Tiwari, also features a large ensemble cast, including Ravie Dubey, Sunny Deol, Arun Govil, Lara Dutta, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, and Kunal Kapoor. Ramayana Part One is slated to rollout worldwide on November 6, ahead of Diwali.

As per the latest buzz, But before that, Yash will be seen in Geetu Mohandas' Toxic, a gangster drama that also stars Kiara Advani, Nayanthara, Tara Sutaria, Rukmini Vasanth, and Huma Qureshi. The movie releases on August 26.

In further updates, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Movie Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera). With a good understanding of cinema and its trends, and a keen eye for detail, he continues to spark conversations around showbiz for readers around the world. Read More

title: Protest, enrolment ‘freeze’, CJI’s rap, then apology: Blow-by-blow of NALSAR row
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Bar Council of India (BCI) has been embroiled in a row of late over its order to freeze the enrolment of the entire 2026 graduating batch of NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad. While the a move that was later rolled back amid backlash, the row continues to simmer.

Adding to this, BCI chairman Manan Kumar Mishra (L) on Saturday apologised over the enrollment move after CJI Surya Kant (R) criticized the Bar Council. In a fresh, BCI chairman Manan Kumar Mishra on Saturday apologised to the law students and shared he sincerely regretted if anything connected with the row, including his words or letter, had hurt their feelings. This was preceded by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant rapping the BCI for its intervention in the NALSAR University of Law enrolment row.

Meanwhile, The National Academy for Legal Studies and Research University, or NALSAR, is a public law school in Hyderabad, Telangana. NALSAR is also among the various national law Universities across India.
Notably, Here is a look back at how the NALSAR-BCI-CJI row unfolded over the past few weeks:

As per the latest buzz, A group of NALSAR students opposed the proposed participation of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as the chief guest at the university’s convocation. They wrote to the vice-chancellor, registrar, and professors voicing their objection.

In further updates, The first representation was submitted on July 23 by 70 members of the outgoing LLB batch. Students from several later batches subsequently expressed their support for the representation, HT reported earlier .

On top of that, In an email sent to the university officials, students raised their objection as they cited the refusal of the Supreme Court bench, led by CJI Kant, to hear a plea regarding the alleged police brutality against students during the July 20 ‘Chalo Sansad’ march in New Delhi's Jantar Mantar.

"As students of law, our concern is narrower and more specific to us as a graduating batch. A convocation is meant to be a moment where the University's own values, including a commitment to constitutional rights, access to justice, and reasoned engagement with grievances, are visibly reflected in the choices it makes," the students wrote in their email, as per news agency PTI.

title: Batwara 1947 box office collection day 2: Sunny Deol film recovers after Awarapan 2 onslaught with massive 135% jump
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Batwara 1947 ticket-window earnings day 2: It was a tough day for Batwara 1947 on Friday. The movie had the combined might of Sunny Deol and Rajkumar Santoshi, and was backed by Aamir Khan’s production house. Yet, it met the wave of Emraan Hashmi ’s renaissance, and Awarapan 2 demolished it. But Saturday was another story. The Partition drama recovered like few films can, registering a strong day 2, and raising hopes for a healthy opening weekend.

Adding to this, Batwara 1947 ticket-window earnings day 2: Sunny Deol in a still from the movie. Batwara 1947 ticket-window update Batwara 1947 was always trailing in this box-office clash. The movie has collected only ₹ 1.76 crore rupees in advance bookings for day 1, trailing Awarapan’s impressive ₹ 8+ crore rupees. On the rollout day, the same trend continued. Despite favourable reviews and praise for Sunny Deol and Shabana Azmi’s performances, Batwara 1947 opened at just ₹ 5.75 crore rupees net in India, just one-fourth of what Awarapan 2 managed. However, on Saturday, Batwara 1947 recovered strongly as positive word of mouth finally kicked in for the Rajkumar Santoshi movie. On Saturday, Batwara 1947 showed a remarkable 135% jump over its Friday numbers, minting ₹ 13.50 crore rupees. Its total India collection now stands at ₹ 19.25 crore rupees in two days, and it is looking set to cross ₹ 35 crore rupees in its opening weekend if the momentum holds.

Meanwhile, Batwara 1947 was the lowest-opening solo movie by Sunny Deol since his 2018 box-office dud Bhaiaji Superhit. But its recovery on Saturday means it may escape the same fate. The movie also showed remarkable growth in occupancy across India. On Friday, its occupancy levels were dismal at 7-12% for the day shows, only to rise to a somewhat respectable 25% for the night shows. But on Saturday, occupancy hovered between 38% and 46% across the day, evening, and night shows.

Notably, In Batwara 1947, Sunny Deol plays a Muslim man who migrates to Pakistan during the Partition. However, he discovers a Hindu woman, played by Shabana Azmi, living upstairs in his home, who refuses to leave. He takes it upon himself to protect her while also ensuring his family's safety amid the chaos. Batwara 1947 sees Preity Zinta return to the big screen after almost a decade. The movie also marks the first on-screen collaboration between Sunny and his son, Karan Deol, who plays his son on screen. The cast also includes Ali Fazal, Abhimanyu Singh, Khushi Hajare, and Kanikka Kapur.

title: Saiyami Kher opens up on returning to IFFM with Pal Bhar Ke Liye, says the film ‘really moved’ her | Interview
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Saiyami Kher is all set to return to the International Movie Festival of Melbourne (IFFM), this time with her soon-to-release movie Pal Bhar Ke Liye. Directed by debutant filmmaker and veteran fashion designer Vikram Phadnis, the movie also stars Tahir Raj Bhasin and Vineet Kumar Singh in pivotal roles. It will have its world premiere at IFFM on August 16.

Adding to this, Saiyami Kher talks about her movie Pal Bhar Ke Liye's world premiere at IFFM. In an interview with Hindustan Times, Saiyami Kher opened up about returning to IFFM with Pal Bhar Ke Liye after Ghoomer. She reflected that the experience feels less stressful this time around and opened up that the movie moved her while challenging her as an star. She also spoke about her experience working with co-stars Tahir Raj Bhasin and Vineet Kumar Singh.

Meanwhile, Talking about the movie, Saiyami says, “Pal Bhar Ke Liye is a movie that Vikram Phadnis is directing, and it's his debut movie. He's been a fashion designer for 35 years and has done costumes for so many iconic films. The movie is about this very ambitious fashion photographer, whom I am playing. She is the best in the business and is doing well in her life until something happens and her whole life turns upside down, and she realises the importance of relationships and family. That's why the title, in a split second, life changes. Both Vineet and Tahir are playing very crucial parts in the movie, and I was genuinely happy to work with them.”

Notably, For Saiyami, returning to IFFM brings back special memories of Ghoomer, which was the festival's opening movie. “It's very exciting to go back. Ghoomer was the opening movie, and it was very special. But it was all a blur that time because we did the screening and flew out the same night, because Ghoomer was releasing just three days later in India. But this time we are more relaxed about going in, watching other films, and attending the festival properly. It's not as stressful as it was last time,” she shared.

As per the latest buzz, She is particularly excited to see Pal Bhar Ke Liye screened for the public. She added, “I'm very excited because this time the movie is going to be shown to the public, and it's always this nervous excitement when your movie is shown publicly for the first time. It feels very special.”

In further updates, Saiyami admitted that following Ghoomer, she was looking for a role that could challenge her in a different way. “For me, I was so invested in Ghoomer, and it was very difficult for a movie to top that role emotionally and physically. But I think Pal Bhar Ke Liye really moved me. I was very overwhelmed with the narration itself. The movie is very emotional, and it made me slow down and think about my life personally and how things can change so quickly and how we take things for granted.”
On top of that, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Indian Movie Festival of Melbourne (@iffmelbourne)
She added, “This movie made me very emotional as a person. And as an star, it is a very layered role; it was a very challenging role. The script and the role were the hero.”

title: Govinda slams wife Sunita Ahuja over abusive remarks: ‘You have made the name of mothers and sisters very cheap’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The war of words between star Govinda and his wife, Sunita Ahuja , shows no signs of dying down. After calling out Sunita for maligning his name and causing a hindrance to his soon-to-release projects, the star has now criticized his wife for using abusive language in front of the camera.

Adding to this, Govinda calls out Sunita Ahuja for using abusive language. 'Everyone will see your real face' In a recent video shared by a paparazzo, Govinda called out Sunita for openly using abusive language. He shared, "Sunita ji aap bahut zyada maa-behen ki gaaliyan dene lagi hai (Sunita ji you are abusing a lot these days). If people get inspired by you...everyone will see your real face. Youngsters will look at you, and the way you behave, they will follow it. What if people start abusing you like that? We will be embarrassed if that happens. Don't do this. You have made the name of mothers and sisters vey cheap. This is not expected from you."
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Varinder Chawla (@varindertchawla)

Notably, Sunita had earlier reacted to Govinda's appearance with star Komal Rani Swarnkar and questioned his decision to be seen with her. She shared, “The picture must be made first (laughs). Promotions occur after a movie is made. But without promotions…now what can I say? He’s roaming with a girl his daughter’s age; he should be ashamed. He must have a standard. Your sugar daddy is so rich; at least dress properly. Look at us dressed so stylishly.) Very bad, he’s lost his mind.”

As per the latest buzz, In another paparazzo video, Govinda criticised Sunita for allegedly using him and asking him to come on cooking show and Lock Upp for her own benefit. He also accused her of sabotaging his soon-to-release projects and attempting to damage his reputation.

In further updates, He shared, "But now that I have started a movie, you are leaving no stone unturned to make me lose people's respect, defame me or do something that could affect my business. People from poor families come into the movie industry; please don't humiliate or defame them to such an extent that they run away or become afraid. You have the ability, power, wealth and respect. God has given you everything. But that doesn't mean you should humiliate someone who doesn't have these things. It doesn't suit you."

On top of that, Govinda also reacted to Sunita calling him a "sugar daddy" and defended his decision to work with younger female actors. He shared, "Actors across the country have worked with young female actors. They got good films, fame and respect, and they also got opportunities to work with younger actors, which is why they continue to look young. You do not want me to look young."

title: Jharkhand protesters threaten to gherao CM Soren's residence, demand his resignation
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The job aspirants protesting against alleged irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) examinations on Saturday opened up that they would gherao chief minister Hemant Soren’s official residence on August 20, demanding his resignation .

Adding to this, A drone view shows job aspirants and students taking out a massive 'Tiranga Yatra' procession to protest against the Jharkhand government over the JPSC and JSSC-CGL exam paper leak issues, at Albert Ekka Chowk, in Ranchi. (PTI) Seeking “accountability” for the irregularities, spokesperson of the “JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch”, Piyush Singh, shared: “This is the first time we are making this demand. It’s time that accountability must also be fixed for the scams”.
Meanwhile, Students protesting against alleged irregularities in the examinations took out a ‘Tiranga Yatra’ on Saturday -- the 22nd day of the indefinite strike started by the students.

Notably, “We have been pleading the government in a Gandhian way till now. But our demands have been falling on deaf ear. We are today announcing to gherao the chief minister residence on August 20. We are reiterating our demands to cancel JSSC -CGL exam and order CBI inquiry. If they don’t, we will march to the chief minister residence and keep sitting there until our demands are met,” Singh told reporters.
As per the latest buzz, Protesting students also demanded Congress to withdraw support from JMM-led coalition.

In further updates, JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch leader Ravindra Paswan shared: “We will gherao the chief minister’s residence on August 20. We seek his resignation as both the JMM and the Congress are playing politics with us. We also demand that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi withdraw support from the JMM-led coalition if the CM is not listening to him.” “Rahul Gandhi spoke to us on phone. But such symbolisms won’t work anymore...”
On top of that, The protesting students have been demanding a CBI investigation or an inquiry by a panel of retired judges from outside Jharkhand into the alleged irregularities.

Stationed in Ranchi, Vishal is heading the Jharkhand Bureau of Hindustan Times since November 2017. Besides leading the reporting team, Vishal tracks and writes on developments related to the state politics, economy and policy matters in Jharkhand. Prior to his current assignment, Vishal used to work in New Delhi after graduating from the University of Delhi. Vishal joined HT in the rank of Assistant Editor in August 2015 and was part of the Delhi Metro Bureau, covering a host of issues in the City-state including politics, policy---especially those related to urban traffic & transport infrastructure and railways. A native of Palamu district in Jharkhand, Vishal started his two-decade long career in the mainstream media in 2006. During this period, he has has worked in different capacity with a number of national media houses including the Financial Chronicle, India Today, Deccan Herald and The Hindu, before moving to the Hindustan Times. He holds the experience of having worked in three major mediums of mass communication--Print, Electronic and Digital. He is a proud father of two daughters. Read More

Share Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Email Copy Copied Batwara 1947 Ticket-window Day 2 (Early Trends): Sunny Deol’s Dhai Kilo Ka Haath Finally Making An Impact! (Photo Credit: YouTube) After a surprisingly low opening day, Sunny Deol’s theatrical power has roared back at the ticket counters! Director Rajkumar Santoshi’s ambitious Partition saga, Batwara 1947, registered a remarkable turnaround on Saturday, proving that period dramas hugely rely on positive word-of-mouth and holiday audience to unleash their true potential! In two days, the movie has crossed the 20 crore rupees mark at the ticket-window with its net collection in India!

Adding to this, The stark jump in overall occupancy from 14% on Friday to 34% on Saturday indicates that family audiences have started hitting the theaters to enjoy the partition drama, giving the movie much-needed breath after an initial setback against Awarapan 2. However, it still has a very long way to go since a 19 – 21 crore rupees net collection in 2 days is way underwhelming!

Meanwhile, Following a modest 5.75 crore rupees start on Friday, the movie has witnessed a magical surge of nearly 140% on Day 2. As per early trend estimates for Saturday, August 15, day 2, Batwara 1947 collected in the range of 13 – 15 crore rupees net collection in India! The movie registered an occupancy of 34% for almost 8000 shows in India.

Notably, While the 140% growth brings immense success for producer Aamir Khan , the financial hurdle remains steep for the movie! With a reported budget of 120 crore rupees, the movie’s two-day total in India translates to only 17.5% budget recovery so far.

As per the latest buzz, Sunny Deol ‘s Dhai Kilo Ka Haath has finally asserted its box-office presence with a strong 13–15 crore rupees performance on Saturday. title: ‘Art has to suffer because of politics’: Mustafa Zahid says it's 'unfortunate' to not be part of Awarapan 2 album
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Indian audiences were introduced to Pakistani singer Mustafa Zahid when he sang Awarapan's tracks Toh Phir Aao and Tera Mera Rishta. The songs became the soul of the movie and also played a major role in helping it attain cult status. However, after almost two decades, when the movie's sequel, Awarapan 2 , has been rolled out in theatres, Mustafa's voice is missing from the movie.

Adding to this, Mustafa Zahid opened up on not being part of Awarapan 2. Mustafa on not being part of Awarapan 2 At a recent concert in Chicago, the singer addressed his absence from the movie's tracks, which have been recreated by different singers. He expressed his discontent at not being part of the movie. Addressing his audience at the concert, he shared, "This is the first song of my life that I wrote. This is the first song of my life that I composed and it happens to be the first song that I sang in my life. It is unfortunate that sometimes art has to suffer because of all the politics around the world. So, unfortunately, I am not part of the album, but the amount of love and respect that I have always received from the Indians is absolutely amazing. Thank you so much guys."
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Abbas Khan Jadoon (@abbas_.jadoon)

Notably, The songs proved to be a major turning point in Mustafa's career. The overwhelming response to his music in Awarapan led him to sing in several other Bollywood films, including Blood Money, Aashiqui 2 and Ek Villain, among others.

As per the latest buzz, Mustafa is likely absent from the sequel's album because of the long-standing restrictions on Pakistani artists working in the Indian movie industry. Earlier, veteran lyricist Sayeed Quadri reacted to Mustafa’s absence from the music album of Awarapan 2. He told News18, “Bahot saari cheeze hoti hai jo haalat and waqt ko dekh ke karni padhti hai (There are a lot of things that one has to do seeing the current situation and time). The most important thing is that nation should always come first. Desh sarvapari hai."

In further updates, For the unversed, the new version of Tera Mera Rishta has instead been sung by Saaj Bhatt and Subodhh Sharma. Not just Mustafa, Pritam, who had composed the music for the 2007 movie, is also missing from the sequel. Amaal and Mithoon have composed the music for Awarapan 2.

On top of that, Talking about the same, Sayeed had shared, “Writers usually don’t have a say in this matter. So, I can’t say why Pritam isn’t a part of Awarapan 2. This call was taken by the production house. But Mithoon and Amaal have recreated the songs with a lot of heart."

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Mohana, quashed the FIRs and closed proceedings against Samay Raina and four others - .Balraj Ghai, Sonali Thakker, Nishant Tanwar and Vipul Goyal, for their remarks about people with disabilities on the show, India’s Got Latent. The senior advocate appearing for the petitioner foundation acknowledged before the court that the respondents had made genuine efforts to engage, and the Court recorded that it had no reason to doubt they would continue to work towards celebrating the lives and dignity of persons living with SMA.”

title: Jackky Bhagnani returns to acting after six years with Independence Day anthem 'Tere Rang Mein': "I wanted the street credibility and respect of Gen Z"
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bhagnani described himself as a patriot and shared the nature of the song played an important role in his decision to face the camera again. “I am a patriot by heart. It’s been quite some time since I faced the camera. So, I thought the best way to come back is with the right cause,” Bhagnani shared.

Adding to this, The star's return comes after several years of focusing primarily on movie production. According to Bhagnani, stepping away from acting was a conscious decision as he worked behind the scenes and became more involved in producing films.

Meanwhile, Bhagnani shared his experience as a producer made him rethink the way he wanted to approach his acting career. He explained that producing his own films gave him greater control over the projects he wanted to associate with. “I realised that I should produce my own films because if I do that, no one will question it,” he shared.

Notably, The star-producer also spoke about wanting to establish greater credibility among younger audiences. He shared that even when some of his films performed well, he felt he had not received the recognition he was looking for as an star. “I felt that even in the films that were working, I wasn’t getting credibility. I wanted the street credibility and respect of Gen Z, they should see that this is made by me,” Bhagnani shared.

As per the latest buzz, Now that he is returning to acting, Bhagnani shared he is not looking to sign projects simply for the sake of being on screen. Instead, he is searching for a role that offers something different.

In further updates, The star shared he is looking for something “disruptive” for his next acting project, suggesting that his return to films will be guided by the kind of material he finds creatively interesting.

On top of that, Bhagnani also spoke about his wife, star Rakul Preet Singh, who will soon be seen as Surpanakha in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part 1. The star-producer expressed confidence in her performance and shared the movie could introduce another side of her talent to Hindi-speaking audiences. “Rakul is my superstar. She has seen superstardom in the South. She has so much more to offer to the Hindi audience, and Ramayana will do that for her,” he shared.
Bhagnani also acknowledged the challenges involved in portraying a character such as Surpanakha. “Surpanakha can be a tricky character, but she has played it with elegance,” he added.

title: Exclusive| Tara Sutaria opens up on the first Navroz in her own home, shares the festive menu
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Star Tara Sutaria in conversation with HTCity opens up about hosting friends and family for Navroz, at her own home for the first time.

Adding to this, Tara Sutaria, Ses at her home Speaking about playing host this time around Tara says, "I’ve been doing a lot of prep with my house help and ofcourse my mum. I love decor and enjoy using fruits and flowers for my tablescape. I enjoy planning the festive menu. Not a lot of people know much about the Parsi community because it’s a small but great one so talking about it excites me, there’s a lot of sweetness to this culture and most people connect to our love for food.”

Meanwhile, Sharing what's on the menu this year for the celebrations the star says, “We have a dessert called mawa-ni-boi, a fish shaped sweet dish with silver foil that we prepare. In our culture fish signifies prosperity so we have a lot of fish shaped items in Parsi culture to ring in good luck. Even though its New Year and not a wedding, my family prepares lagan nu bhonu on Navroz which translates to wedding feast. This time I’m making Persian inspired dishes like saffron rice with zereshk berries, lamb shanks, all kinds of Parsi food," says the star. About the decor she adds, “Then there’s the ses that we decorate, which is similar to a pooja ki thali from Hindu culture, on a silver platter we keep a lamp, rice, tika and a fish shaped item. There’s a lot of little items that we keep as part of our tradition. ”

Notably, She says that family time during the New Year is most precious. “My twin sister Pia and I often travel to different parts of the world, so Navroz is a time where the family comes together. I don’t live with my parents anymore so this year is extra special. The perfect Navroz celebration would be eating, drinking, just having a good time together," says Tara.

title: Anurag Kashyap shares marriage plans with 20-year-younger GF Shubhra, says he ‘tried to push her away’ after age-shaming
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood filmmaker Anurag Kashyap has been in a relationship with Shubhra Shetty for nearly a decade. In a recent conversation with Janice Sequeira, the filmmaker and Shubhra spoke about their relationship, the scrutiny they have faced because of their age difference and whether marriage is on the cards for them.

Adding to this, Anurag Kashyap says he is at peace since he has been in a relationship with Shubhra Shetty. Anurag Kashyap on whether he wants to get married to Shubhra Shetty When asked about their plans to marry, Anurag opened up that Shubhra doesn't believe in marriage and added, “I’m very happy to be with her. I want to be with her. So, whatever that takes. There’s a lot in life. What is an old man’s insecurity? I want to be healthy enough to outlive the people I love. Because if it doesn’t happen, then what can happen after that? The ways of the world. So, I think about it a lot. But my thing is, as long as we have found what we have found now, I’m happy with anything. I don’t want to lose this.”

Meanwhile, Shubhra recalled that she and Anurag were in their honeymoon phase and deeply in love when she casually mentioned that being in love was on her bucket list and that she could happily die after experiencing it. However, Anurag became emotional and teared up. He told her that before meeting her, he had never been afraid of dying and did not care if he got into a car accident. He shared that, for the first time in his life, he had found something worth living for and therefore did not want to die. Shubhra described it as the sweetest way of looking at their relationship.

Notably, Anurag shared that the age-shaming no longer follows them, although they have had their "share of troubles". He added, "We’ve had our moments. We have been self-conscious. I’ve been more conscious.. And not just more conscious, at one point, I became so conscious, I was trying so hard to push it away. There was a point because her face doesn’t show her age. She still looks the same. She doesn’t look her age. So the thing is, the more I grew older and she kept looking the same, that’s when I became slightly conscious.” While Anurag is 53 years old, Shubhra opened up that she is in her 30s.

As per the latest buzz, Shubhra Shetty previously worked as an assistant director at Anurag's production company, Phantom Films. Anurag was first photographed with Shubhra in 2015, but it was only in a 2018 interview that he first admitted to being in a relationship with her.

In further updates, Before his relationship with Shubhra, Anurag was married to editor Aarti Bajaj. The couple ended their six-year marriage in 2009 and share a daughter, Aaliyah Kashyap. Anurag later began dating star Kalki Koechlin, whom he married in 2011. They ended their marriage after four years.

title: Ramayana English trailer: Namit Malhotra DECODES DNEG’s AI-powered lip-sync technology!
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Unlike conventional dubbed versions, where a new voice track is placed over the original footage, the English version of Ramayana: Part 1 uses DNEG’s AI-powered technology to digitally adjust the actors’ mouth movements. Producer Namit Malhotra has now explained how the process combines human performances with technology to achieve a more natural result.

Adding to this, In conversation with ET Now, Malhotra stressed that the process did not begin with AI. According to the producer, the first step involved human voice performances, with members of the principal cast also contributing their own English voices.

Meanwhile, “If you've seen that, where we've got tremendous praise, where we've actually brought in human actors, voice actors, who actually come in and performed the voice performances. Some of them actually are done by the actors themselves, who have a good command over the language and are able to emote appropriately in a different language,” he shared.

Notably, Malhotra explained that this human-led approach was important to preserve the emotional quality of the performances. “So we've done that as a first step to make sure that the rendering of that expression and emotion is authentic, and it's led by humans. There is no AI whatsoever,” he added.

As per the latest buzz, The next stage involved creating the appropriate lip movements for the English dialogue. Malhotra shared human artists first established the foundation for how the characters’ lips should move in sync with the new voice performances.

In further updates, “There is no AI whatsoever. We followed that up with what we're calling, because we are trying to make the lip sync in line with the voice. So we have a next step, which is again done by humans, where you actually have people coming in, what we call a human driver that actually creates this foundation of how the lips actually move and how it syncs itself to the voice itself,” he explained.

On top of that, According to Malhotra, the challenge was not simply matching a voice to an star. The team also had to ensure that the voice performance, facial appearance and lip movements worked together convincingly.

“And it looks appropriate because the best voice star may not have the right face for the star on screen. So we are making sure that you've got the voice actors, we've got people whose faces and lips match the look of the actors,” Malhotra shared.

title: Devendra Mahto stopped from Tiranga Yatra by police in Jharkhand. He protests from hospital floor | Watch
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Student Leader Devendra Nath Mahto , was allegedly stopped by the police from participating in a Tiranga Yatra being carried out by student protestors in Ranchi on the occasion of Independence Day. Mahto, who is the leader of Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM), is currently admitted in Sadar Hospital.

Adding to this, Mahto protests from hospital floor (Screen Grab) In an X post on Saturday Mahto expressed his desire to peacefully participate in the flag hoisting and Tricolor March organized at the protest site, Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium but was forced back into his hospital room by police officers. He also added that heavy police deployment could be seen outside his room.
Meanwhile, He questioned, "What kind of freedom is this, after all? Are we not even free to hoist the Tricolor and participate in the Tricolor March in our own country?"
Notably, Mahto has shared multiple videos of the incident.
As per the latest buzz, In one video he shared on X, Mahto is seen being pushed and shoved into his hospital room by police as he tries to fight it. He's wearing a tricolour scarf and bandana.

In further updates, He shared that the police tried to forcefully stop him along with his companions, from joining the Tiranga Yatra. “Despite being hungry for several days, I stand firm for my rights and the voice of the people. They cannot silence our voice by stopping us in this manner.” He added.

On top of that, In another video shared on X by Mahto, he is seen lying on the hospital floor backed by his companions. He shared that the police kept pushing and shoving him to stop him from leaving until he finally sat down right outside his room's gate.

Mahto shared, “Until I'm allowed to leave from here, I'll keep sitting right here. I won't even get my treatment done, and I'll stay here to make my point. My fight is for the rights of the people and for justice. They can't silence my voice by stopping me.”

title: Govinda warns wife Sunita Ahuja after her ‘sugar daddy’ jibe, claims she is backed by gang: ‘Aap apni hadh mein rahein’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Govinda of late made headlines after he was spotted at Mumbai airport with a young female co-star, prompting social media users to speculate that she was his girlfriend. His wife, Sunita Ahuja , reacted to the video with blunt remarks, calling Govinda a "sugar daddy". Now, Govinda has hit back at Sunita's comments and warned her to "stay in her limits".

Adding to this, Govinda hits back at Sunita Ahuja's remarks. Govinda reacts to wife Sunita Ahuja calling him Komal Rani's ‘sugar daddy’ Govinda was seen in conversation with a paparazzo, where he criticised Sunita's remarks and accused her of having him called on both the cooking show and Lock Upp for her own benefit, adding that she had every right to do so. He shared, "But now that I have started a movie, you are leaving no stone unturned to make me lose people's respect, defame me or do something that could affect my business. People from poor families come into the movie industry; please don't humiliate or defame them to such an extent that they run away or become afraid. You have the ability, power, wealth and respect. God has given you everything. But that doesn't mean you should humiliate someone who doesn't have these things. It doesn't suit you."
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by TAHIR JASUS007 (@tahirjasus)

Notably, He further reacted to Sunita calling him a "sugar daddy" and criticising him for working with an star his daughter's age. Govinda shared, "Actors across the country have worked with young female actors. They got good films, fame and respect, and they also got opportunities to work with younger actors, which is why they continue to look young. You do not want me to look young."

As per the latest buzz, Govinda then warned Sunita, "Aapke peeche jo group aur gang hai usse sabhi waqif hain aur voh jaldi khulke aage aajayegi. Aur aage bhi aapko shayad meri zarurat pad sakti hai toh aap kripya aise bayan deke aur yeh podcast chalake beizzati kiye jaa rahi hain, aap thoda sa apni hadh mein rahiye (Everyone is aware of the group and gang behind you, and they will soon come out in the open. You may need me in the future as well, so please stop making such statements and running this podcast to humiliate me. Please know your limits)."

In further updates, Sunita had reacted to Govinda's appearance with star Komal Rani Swarnkar and shared, “The picture must be made first (laughs). Promotions occur after a movie is made. But without promotions…now what can I say? He’s roaming with a girl his daughter’s age; he should be ashamed. He must have a standard. Your sugar daddy is so rich; at least dress properly. Look at us dressed so stylishly.) Very bad, he’s lost his mind.”
On top of that, A report by Moneycontrol suggested that Govinda will star alongside Komal in his soon-to-release films Roopa and Duniyadari.

Govinda and Sunita have been married since 1987 and have two children, Tina and Yashvardhan. This is not the first time that the star has been accused of being unfaithful in the relationship. During her stint on Lock Upp Season 2, Sunita admitted that Govinda had had multiple affairs.

Awarapan 2 ticket-window update till 5 PM Awarapan 2 opened at ₹ 22 crore rupees net on Friday, the best opening of Emraan Hashmi’s career, and one of the biggest debuts by a Hindi movie this year. The movie started slowly on Friday morning but built steadily, with the evening shows registering a staggering 74% occupancy. On Saturday, even the morning shows delivered better returns than on Friday. According to Sacnilk, Awarapan 2 collected around ₹ 15.21 crore rupees at the net ticket-window by 5 pm on its second day. This gives the movie a total two-day haul of just over ₹ 37.21 crore rupees. On Saturday, Awarapan 2 registered 32% occupancy across India for its morning shows, which jumped to 70% for the afternoon shows. The numbers are expected to increase further during the evening and night shows.

Meanwhile, Awarapan 2 has been selling over 20k tickets per hour on BookMyShow all through Friday and Saturday. This is a remarkable pace for any movie without a superstar. On Friday, it took the sequel all of eight hours to overtake the lifetime business of the first Awarapan. The 2007 ticket-window dud had collected just ₹ 7.75 crore rupees net. By Saturday afternoon, the movie was surpassing the final collections of even the hit films Emraan Hashmi has given. It has already surpassed the likes of Haq ( ₹ 20 crore rupees), Raaz 2 ( ₹ 25.50 crore rupees), Ek Thi Daayan ( ₹ 26 crore rupees), and Jannat ( ₹ 30 crore rupees).

title: ‘Decided to be relevant again’: Comedian Daniel Fernandes takes a dig at Bhumi Pednekar over Delhi protest remarks
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bhumi Pednekar received a lot of flak after she schooled protesters during the CJP-led protest in Delhi for using abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi . Of late, comedian Daniel Fernandes also took a dig at the star over her comments and questioned her take on relating the protesters' language to culture.

Adding to this, Comedian Daniel Fernandes takes a swipe at Bhumi Pednekar. 'Culture is spelled as CONTROL' During his stand-up show, Daniel shared, " Bhumi Pednekar woke up one morning and decided to be relevant again. So, she posted a video where she is like, 'Hey guys, it is okay to protest and all that, but what is this language? This bad, abusive language is not part of our culture. Not part of our culture? What are you, French? Remembering mothers and sisters is a national pastime. This is what society does: every time they do not like something that you say or do, they will try to shame you by saying that this is not part of our culture and culture is spelled as 'CONTROL'. I don't understand what is up with this a** kissing."

Meanwhile, The comedian also brought up TV star Sudesh Berry's recent comment in an interview, during which he shared he wanted to wash the Prime Minister's feet and drink that water. "He has not understood Swachh Bharat Abhiyan," the comedian shared in a swipe at him.

Notably, Earlier, Bhumi had criticised protesters for using abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Her remarks led many to question why the star had not supported the student-led CJP protest in Delhi, which had demanded the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan following the NEET paper leak and other examination irregularities, but had instead decided to school protesters about their behaviour.

As per the latest buzz, Bhumi had shared in the clip, "Looking at the videos surfacing now, the kind of language being used, and the way the youth of our country are speaking — the youth of our country... this isn't how we talk, man. We are talking about someone who holds the highest office in the land today. And it’s not just about the office; would we ever speak like this to the elders in our own homes? Can we really resort to using abusive language?”

In further updates, She added, "Guys, this isn't our culture; it’s wrong, and this really bothered me — that’s why I wanted to come forward and address this: a country will only progress and move forward when, collectively and unitedly, we discuss our flaws as well as the good things. Our culture and value system form our backbone; we shouldn't stray from them, otherwise, we won't be able to communicate the right things in the right way, and they will never be implemented or lead to change."

On top of that, Bhumi was last seen in the web show Daldal, which received underwhelming reviews from critics and audiences alike. She also starred in the 2025 movie Mere Husband Ki Biwi, which left theatres without making much of a mark.

title: ‘He is greedy’: Priyadarshan on directing Saif Ali Khan in Haiwaan for first time, says he asks a lot of questions
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Priyadarshan collaborated with Bollywood star Saif Ali Khan for the first time in Haiwaan . In a recent interview with Pinkvilla, the filmmaker opened up about his experience working with Saif, describing him as a 'greedy but obedient' star and revealing how the star developed a certain level of confidence in him.

Adding to this, Priyadarshan opens up about directing Saif Ali Khan in Haiwaan. Priyadarshan on directing Saif Ali Khan in Haiwaan Calling Saif a "mature child", Priyadarshan shared, "He has a lot of questions every time, and of course every star has the right but the question; the moment it is answered, he just obeys you. After two days, I found that there was no question, so I asked him in the morning, ‘Any questions?’ He shared, ‘No sir, now I know what you want to shoot.’ So that actually builds our confidence with each other, and that is the way it went on. Saif is too committed."

Meanwhile, He further shared a habit of Saif's that he described as "difficult" to find among actors today, reading books between shots instead of being glued to his phone. Priyadarshan added that Saif is a voracious reader with an impressive knowledge of the world around him.

Notably, Priyadarshan added, “I could discuss a lot of things with him because I am a huge Pataudi Nawab fan, so I spent a lot of time with him. He also gifted me a nice book with an autograph of Pataudi, so I really enjoyed being with him. I found him a very obedient star, a little greedy but a very obedient star, so that is the best part about him. I think he developed a certain kind of confidence in me, which really helped me to take the movie forward in a very smooth way.”

As per the latest buzz, The teaser of the movie opened up that Saif plays the role of a visually impaired man. He is seen walking with a stick and wearing a special watch for the visually impaired. The teaser also showed Akshay Kumar's character walking menacingly before letting out a sinister laugh. Haiwaan also features an ensemble cast including Boman Irani, Saiyami Kher and Shriya Pilgaonkar in pivotal roles.

In further updates, Produced by Venkat K. Narayana and Shailaja Desai Fenn under KVN Productions and Thespian Films, the movie marks Akshay and Saif's reunion after 18 years. The two were last seen together in the 2008 movie Tashan. Priyadarshan previously opened up that Haiwaan is a remake of the Malayalam movie Oppam, although several changes have been made to the dialogues and screenplay. He has also teased Mohanlal's cameo in the movie. Haiwaan is scheduled to rollout in theatres on September 11, 2026.

title: Baba Ramdev throws surprise demand for educational reforms, threatens to go on protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Just after the Cockroach Janta Party raised the issue of lack of proper infrastructure in schools and sought reforms under its 'School Thik Karo' campaign, famed yoga guru Baba Ramdev on Saturday made similar remarks on the state of education and schools in the country.

Adding to this, Baba Ramdev (in picture) that students from smaller schools are complaining about the lack of basics such as teachers, electricity an water. (ANI) Ramdev also threatened to go on a protest over his demands of educational reforms, saying that students from smaller schools are complaining about the lack of basics such as teachers, electricity and water. In his remarks, Ramdev also mentioned the paper leaks, an issue that of late sparked massive youth-led protests across the country which culminated in the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister.

Meanwhile, “There is chaos all over the country. Children are leaving small schools, complaining that they have no teachers, no electricity, no water, no toilets. There are books, but there are teachers; there are teachers, but there are no books. Even if there are books, the papers are leaked. The 10th and 12th grade board exams are not included anywhere. Admissions are based solely on competitive exams,” Ramdev was quoted as saying by Live Hindustan.
Notably, While making the remarks at an Independence Day event, Ramdev alleged that 90 to 99 percent of the time, interviews for government jobs are ‘fraudulent.’

As per the latest buzz, “They recruit people from their own background, ideology, culture, organization, caste, and class, and push away the rest. On one hand, we proclaim that truth prevails, yet when it comes to recruitment, it's already decided. They charge crores of rupees.”

In further updates, Maintaining that he doesn't support anarchy in the name of protests, Ramdev shared, “How will the country function if we have to resort to protests like this? So, improve yourselves, or there could be more protests in the country. I don't support anarchy in the name of protests. But there's a lot of corruption in the country. It's possible that Ramdev will have to protest again."

On top of that, While Ramdev backed the demands of students for exam reforms, he also made sharp remarks against the Gen Z saying that they have ‘multiple boyfriends and girlfriends’ and are into smoking and drinking.

“Many Gen Zs are doing well also, but some are into violence, have multiple boyfriends or girlfriends. Some are into smoking bidis and cigarettes and drinking alcohol. All we are saying is that get rid of the bad and take forward the good deeds,” Ramdev shared.

title: Clash between police and protesters in Haryana on Independence Day triggers unrest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Tension prevailed in Haryana's Jind district on Saturday after a confrontation between police and protesters in Hansi, with farmers and khap representatives blocking a road at Gulkani village after they were stopped from proceeding towards Hansi to protest against Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini's Independence Day programme.

Adding to this, The protesters were attempting to enter Hansi to demonstrate against the Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini's programme. (HT Archive) The protesters were attempting to enter Hansi to demonstrate against the Chief Minister's programme. However, police stopped them at Gulkani village before they could enter Hansi's limits. Following the intervention, farmers and khap representatives gathered at the spot and blocked the road.

Meanwhile, A heavy police deployment was made in Gulkani to prevent the protesters from moving towards Hansi and to maintain law and order. The situation remained tense following the earlier confrontation between police and protesters in Hansi.

Notably, The protest is linked to anger among farmers and khap organisations over the recent killing of dairy operator Jeevan Kundu. Farmers' unions and khap panchayats had revealed plans to protest at Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini's Independence Day programme in Hansi over the murder.
As per the latest buzz, As a result of the protest call, the Khatakhat toll plaza was also shut on Saturday, adding to the disruption amid the demonstrations by farmers and khap groups.

In further updates, A mahapanchayat of khap panchayats and farmers' unions had revealed a protest at the Chief Minister's Independence Day event. The mahapanchayat had demanded action against all those accused in the killing of Jeevan Kundu, a dairy operator from Surya Nagar. Kundu was allegedly attacked by a group of men with sticks on August 4 and later died during treatment.

On top of that, The murder has triggered anger among sections of farmers and khap organisations, who have raised questions over law and order and demanded strict action against everyone involved in the killing.

BJP MLA Devender Chaturbhuj Attri condemned the murder and expressed condolences to the victim's family. He also criticised what he described as misleading information being circulated on social media.

title: Vikrant Massey says he received threats, his WhatsApp number was leaked after The Sabarmati Report: ‘Listened to abuses’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Vikrant Massey has opened up about the toll social media criticism once took on his emotional and mental health. The star, who is currently receiving appreciation for his performance in Musafir Cafe , of late appeared on Shekhar Suman 's talk show and recalled facing abuse, threats and the leaking of his personal details after the rollout of The Sabarmati Report. He also opened up that the backlash came at a particularly difficult time, when his son was just six months old.

Adding to this, Vikrant Massey on social media toxicity. Vikrant Massey on receiving threats after The Sabarmati Report Vikrant talked about the growing toxicity on social media, recalling how it impacted his emotional and mental health. He shared, “I did a movie called The Sabarmati Report, and I am extremely proud of that movie. When I did that movie, people used the word you used, propaganda. People called that movie propaganda. We made it on the Godhra train burning. We made it on the burning of the Sabarmati Express. I had to listen to a lot of abuse. My WhatsApp number was leaked. My car number was leaked. People threatened me openly.”

Meanwhile, He further explained that the time was particularly difficult for him because his son was just six months old and shared, “My son had just been born then. He was just six months old. I was heavily impacted, and I openly shared this in the media. However, over time, I realised that they are all cowards, and it doesn’t matter to me what people talk about me. What matters is that my own people are my responsibility. I am answerable to them.”

Notably, The Sabarmati Report is a 2024 Hindi political thriller directed by Dheeraj Sarna and starring Vikrant Massey, Raashii Khanna and Ridhi Dogra in key roles. The movie is inspired by the 27 February 2002 burning of the Sabarmati Express at Godhra, Gujarat, in which 59 people died. It was rolled out in theatres on 15 November 2024.

As per the latest buzz, The story follows journalist Samar Kumar, played by Vikrant Massey, who is sent to Godhra to report on the tragedy. Years later, journalist Amrita Gill, played by Raashii Khanna, discovers Samar's old report and joins him in investigating what happened.

In further updates, After the success of Musafir Cafe Season 1, Netflix has renewed the show for a second season. Vikrant will reprise his role as Chander alongside Vedika Pinto, Mahima Makwana, Siddhartha, Anubha Fatehpuria, Loveleen Mishra and Sadia Siddiqui. The show is currently in production, with the emotional finale of the first season raising expectations for the second season.

title: From Upkar to Dhurandhar: How Bollywood's language of patriotism moved from defiance to pride | Independence Day Special
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Patriotism in Hindi cinema began during the British Raj, with songs like Door Hato Ae Duniya Walon defying British censors and introducing nationalism to cinema. But over the years, the most popular lines and songs about patriotism in Bollywood have shifted from defiance to pride and, eventually, to swag.

Adding to this, Aditya Dhar's Dhurandhar The Revenge contained an aggressive, proud tone of patriotism. Defiance against the ‘masters’ - the beginnings The 1943 movie Kismet was one of the first Hindi films to include a song or theme that one can call patriotic and nationalistic. Up until then, patriotism was introduced through historical accounts of Akbar, Ashoka, or Shivaji. But Kismet brought nationalism to a movie set during World War II.

Meanwhile, When lyrics to a song went ‘ Aaj Himalaya ki choti se humne phir lalkaara hai, door hato ae duniya walon, Hindustan hamara hai’, it was a clarion call to Indians. The movie's makers deftly hid the song from the British censors, saying it was a message to the enemies of British India during the War. But the message reached the masses.

Notably, The early patriotic films were either war dramas or retellings of the freedom struggle. Haqeeqat retold stories from the 1962 China War, while Shaheed was an ode to Bhagat Singh and his comrades. The songs and lines were bold and defiant.

As per the latest buzz, In the 60s, Manoj Kumar took it upon himself to bring a new style of patriotism - pride in what a young India had achieved and hope for the future. From that was born ‘ Mere desh ki dharti sona ugle’ in Upkar. In Purab Aur Pachhim, when he sang ‘ Hai preet jahan ki reet sada,’ the message was clear: India wants to spread love and harmony. Sunil Dutt's Hum Hindustani was a similar love letter to a developing India, with loads of messages of gratitude to Pandit Nehru's administration.

In further updates, According to screenwriter Shantanu Srivastava, the language of patriotism changed because the audience changed. “As the nation grows more self-reliant and prosperous, you also start feeling emotionally involved with patriotism because, after all, being an Indian is my identity. Whenever you see the tricolour or the national anthem plays, you get goosebumps,” he told ANI.

On top of that, There was yet another transition in the 80s as Hindi cinema entered its commercial masala era. The patriotic films of the time became massier, bigger, and more modern. In Karma, Dilip Kumar merged Seven Samurai's plot with a fight against a terrorist overlord. ‘ Dil diya hai, jaan bhi denge, ae watan tere liye’ signified a shift in how love for the nation was perceived now. Sacrifice, while fighting for the nation, was in.

Manoj Kumar, too, adapted to the new theme. His movie, Kranti, was an action-swashbuckler set in British India and emerged as the biggest box-office hit of the decade. Even the reigning superstar Amitabh Bachchan attempted this new style of patriotism as he fought evils like corruption in Main Azaad Hoon.

title: ‘Chota artist hu, islie nahi bulaya’: Mithun Chakraborty reacts to being snubbed by Kolkata Film Festival organisers
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Padma Bhushan recipient and BJP leader Mithun Chakraborty opened up that he was not invited to the movie festival in Kolkata, despite attending a meeting to mark the birth centenary of Bengali cinema icon Uttam Kumar .

Adding to this, Alipurduar: Star and BJP leader Mithun Chakraborty talked about being snubbed by the Kolkata Movie Festival organisers. (PTI Photo) (PTI) Mithun Chakraborty on Kolkata snub "I wasn't invited to the movie festival," Chakraborty shared while in conversation with the media in Kolkata on Friday. He contrasted the reported snub with an soon-to-release visit to Moscow, saying, “I am going to Moscow now; perhaps they will invite me. They are inviting me to the Moscow Movie Festival. Yet, here in Bengal, I wasn't invited.”

Meanwhile, The 'Disco Dancer' star also suggested that he may have been sidelined as a "minor artist" as he has done a few roles in Bengali cinema, while pointing to the frequent invitations extended to figures who do not have a direct connection with Bengal. “Main bahut chota artiste hoon, shayad isliye nahi bulaya (I am a very minor artiste. Maybe that's why they didn't invite me),” the star added sarcastically.

Notably, The remarks came against the backdrop of preparations for a year-long programme to mark the centenary of Uttam Kumar, widely revered as the "Mahanayak" of Bengali cinema. The cine icon was a major figure in Bengali cinema and also attained success in Hindi films.

As per the latest buzz, Born Arun Kumar Chatterjee on September 3, 1926, Uttam Kumar was an star, director and producer who became one of the most influential figures in Bengali cinema. He died on July 24, 1980, aged 53.

In further updates, His early career included a run of box-office failures that collected him the nickname "Flop Master General". He broke the streak with Basu Paribar in 1952, before Sharey Chuattor (1953) established him as a major star and began his celebrated screen partnership with Suchitra Sen. In 1967, he became the first recipient of the National Movie Award for Best Star for his performances in Anthony Firingee and Chiriyakhana.

On top of that, Last week, Mithun Chakraborty underwent a procedure on Thursday to remove a metal plate that had been implanted following an incident. The procedure was successful, and the star is in a stable condition, they shared. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari visited the star and shared an update on his health on social media.
The star is set to appear in a cameo in Rajinikanth's Jailer 2, which is set for rollout in 2027.

title: Batwara 1947 box office collection day 1: Sunny Deol film drowned by Emraan Hashmi's Awarapan 2, opens at just ₹5.75 cr
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Batwara 1947 ticket-window earnings day 1: The Independence Day weekend is the perfect time to rollout a patriotic Sunny Deol movie. In the recent past, a patriotic holiday has worked for Gadar 2 and Border 2. The makers of Batwara 1947, the star’s Partition-era drama, were probably encouraged by this. What they did not count on was the Emraan Hashmi renaissance. In the end, Batwara 1947 was blanked by Awarapan 2 at the ticket-window, earning just 25% of what the Emraan-starrer made on the same day.

Adding to this, Batwara 1947 ticket-window earnings day 1: Sunny Deol and Preity Zinta in a still from Batwara 1947. Batwara 1947 ticket-window update Batwara 1947 was always trailing in this box-office clash. The movie has collected only ₹ 1.76 crore rupees in advance bookings for day 1, trailing Awarapan’s impressive figure of ₹ 8+ crore rupees. On the rollout day, the same trend continued. Despite favourable reviews and praise for Sunny Deol and Shabana Azmi’s performances, Batwara 1947 could not gather enough momentum at the ticket window. According to Sacnilk, the movie opened at ₹ 5.75 crore rupees net in India, much lower than the ₹ 21 crore rupees Awarapan 2 managed on the same day. It is the lowest-opening solo Sunny Deol movie since his 2018 box-office dud Bhaiaji Superhit, which opened at just ₹ 1 crore rupees. Border 2 and Gadar 2 had opened at ₹ 32 crore rupees and ₹ 40 crore rupees, respectively, signifying a dramatic return to box-office glory for the star in his late 60s.

Meanwhile, Batwara 1947 and Awarapan 2 shared the screens across India neatly, with both films getting almost the same number of shows nationwide. But the Sunny Deol-starrer registered rather low turnout. Its occupancy levels were dismal at 7-12% for the day shows, rising to a somewhat respectable 25% for the night shows. In comparison, the night shows of Awarapan 2 had a 75% occupancy rate.

Notably, In Batwara 1947, Sunny Deol plays a Muslim man who migrates to Pakistan during the Partition. However, he discovers a Hindu woman, played by Shabana Azmi, living upstairs in his home, who refuses to leave. He takes it upon himself to protect her while also ensuring his family's safety amid the chaos. Batwara 1947 sees Preity Zinta return to the big screen after almost a decade. The movie also marks the first on-screen collaboration between Sunny and his son, Karan Deol, who plays his son. The cast also includes Ali Fazal, Abhimanyu Singh, Khushi Hajare, and Kanikka Kapur.

As per the latest buzz, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Movie Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera). With a good understanding of cinema and its trends, and a keen eye for detail, he continues to spark conversations around showbiz for readers around the world. Read More

title: CM Adityanath hails Nana Patekar, reveals actor worked to prevent farmer suicides without publicity
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday lauded star Nana Patekar for his work to help farmers affected by suicides and lauded singer-composer Shankar Mahadevan for giving the Uttar Pradesh Police song "Khaki Ka Sitara" a new identity with his voice.

Adding to this, Star Nana Patekar's efforts were lauded by CM Adityanath. (PTI Photo)(PTI05_18_2026_000238B) (PTI) What did the CM say? Speaking at the song's launch here, Adityanath recalled Patekar's efforts to support farmers in Maharashtra when the state was witnessing widespread farmer suicides. "Nana Patekar is not only an star; he is an equally sensitive human being. When farmers in Maharashtra had started committing suicides on a large scale, the person who extended a helping hand to those farmers was none other than Nana Patekar," Adityanath shared.

Meanwhile, The CM shared he was surprised when Patekar came to meet him and introduced himself while he was working for farmers. "I was very surprised. Such a big star was working for farmers, but it was true," he shared, adding that Patekar had worked quietly "without any publicity or fanfare".

Notably, Adityanath shared the star had also contributed to the Uttar Pradesh Police's cyber-security awareness campaign through a short movie aimed at warning people about threats such as digital arrest scams.

As per the latest buzz, The CM thanked the National Award -winning artist for lending his acting to the police's awareness campaign. Adityanath also lauded Mahadevan, saying his singing style left everyone "enthralled". "His name itself is Shankar and in keeping with his name, he has become a double Shankar -- he is Shankar as well as Mahadev," Adityanath shared, noting that the song's launch coincided with the month of Sawan.
In further updates, He shared the Padma-honoured artist's rendition had given "Khaki Ka Sitara" a new identity and could serve as an inspiration for uniformed forces.

On top of that, IPS officer Rahul Srivastav, who is the Public Relations Officer of Uttar Pradesh Police, scripted the cyber-awareness short movie on 'Digital Arrest', featuring Patekar and directed by acclaimed Bollywood writer-director Raaj Shaandilyaa .

Srivastav also worked as creative director on the UP Police song 'Khaki Ka Sitara' penned by noted poet-lyricist Alok Shrivastav, who attended the event along with star Karan Aanand who played a meaningful role in the song.

For PVR INOX, the collaboration highlights the growing opportunity for powerful, fan-loved IPs to create distinctive theatrical experiences and deepen audience engagement. For Excel Entertainment and Amazon MGM Studios, the partnership reflects the enduring popularity of Mirzapur, and the deep connection audiences have built with its characters, stories and cultural legacy over the years.

Adding to this, Niharika Bijli, Lead - Strategist, PVR INOX Limited shared, “At PVR INOX, we believe the power of cinema lies not just in watching a movie, but in sharing an experience that has the potential to become a cultural moment. Our association with Excel Entertainment and Amazon MGM Studios for Mirzapur is one such moment.
Meanwhile, A post shared by Excel Entertainment (@excelmovies)

Notably, Vishal Ramchandani, CEO of Excel Entertainment, shared: "Over the years, Mirzapur has become a cultural phenomenon with a passionate fan following. As we bring the franchise to theatres, we wanted to announce its arrival in a way that felt true to its scale and spirit. MIRZAPVR is a unique celebration of that moment and a tribute to the audiences who have made Mirzapur what it is today.”

As per the latest buzz, Mirzapur is a landmark franchise that has built an extraordinary connection with audiences over the years, and its arrival on the big screen feels like a natural extension of its intense storytelling, unforgettable characters, and devoted fan base. It presents a unique opportunity to amplify an already iconic world into a larger-than-life cinematic spectacle unlike anything its followers have experienced before.”

In further updates, The MIRZAPVR association will come alive in key PVR INOX cinemas across India, including iconic locations such as Priya Cinema in Delhi, alongside theatres in Mumbai, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Lucknow, and other cities. Presented by Amazon MGM Studios and Excel Entertainment, Mirzapur: The Movie is directed by Gurmmeet Singh, written by Puneet Krishna, and produced by Ritesh Sidhwani and Farhan Akhtar under the banner of Excel Entertainment. The movie is co-produced by Kassim Jagmagia and Vishal Ramchandani. Mirzapur: The Movie releases in cinemas on 4th September 2026.

title: Batwara 1947 review: Shabana Azmi, Sunny Deol deliver a heart-wrenching film centered on the Partition of India
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
2026 has already seen a Partition story reduce audiences to tears with Main Vaapas Aaunga . Now, we have Batwara 1947.

Adding to this, Batwara 1947 review: Sunny Deol, Shabana Azmi and Preity Zinta in a still from the movie. Director Rajkumar Santoshi and lead star Sunny Deol have given us classics such as Ghayal, Damini and Ghatak in the past. This time, the duo turns to the popular play Jis Lahore Nai Dekhya, O Jamyai Nai (Those who haven't seen Lahore, aren't even born yet), adapting it into a full-fledged feature movie. But does Batwara 1947 offer a fresh perspective on Partition, or does it revisit familiar territory we have already seen on screen? Let's find out.

Meanwhile, The story revolves around Sikandar Mirza ( Sunny Deol ) and his family: wife Hamida (Preity G Zinta), son Javed (Karan Deol) and daughter Tanvir (Khushi Hajare), who are forced to flee India overnight in the aftermath of Partition. They arrive in Lahore and are allotted a haveli, only to discover that it is still occupied by its previous owner, a Hindu woman named Durgavati (Shabana Azmi), affectionately called Mai by the mohalla.

Notably, The Mirzas, frustrated, try everything they can to make her leave. But Mai refuses, insisting that she is waiting for her son to return. As tensions rise, Yaqoob (Abhimanyu Singh), an aspiring politician, begins to give the conflict a communal colour, further inflaming an already volatile situation. What happens next forms the crux of the movie.

As per the latest buzz, Rajkumar Santoshi adapts the play beautifully for the big screen. Yet, there is something that keeps the movie from being perfect. Perhaps it is the old-school filmmaker in him that occasionally makes Batwara 1947 feel like either a stage play or an ’80s movie, because the pitch is often louder than it needs to be. For a story largely confined to the physical space of a haveli, the scenes sometimes carry an exaggerated quality. The confrontations are amplified, and the performances are often pitched a notch above what the material demands. It works in parts, but also prevents the movie from achieving the quiet realism that could have made its story even more affecting.

In further updates, Nevertheless, the first half of Batwara 1947 is highly engaging. For those unfamiliar with the source material, the story is likely to feel engrossing. More importantly, the movie makes you think, and think hard. For people who once called a country their home, being forced to leave it overnight, or being told that they no longer belonged there, must have been a trauma beyond our comprehension. Batwara 1947 captures those scars, reminding us that Partition was not merely about the drawing of a new border, but about the lives and homes that were torn apart by it.

On top of that, The second half begins on a slightly shaky note, as the narrative loses some of the momentum it had established in the first half. The pacing becomes a little uneven, with the music dragging down the movie at a few places. However, it soon finds its footing again, largely on the strength of its cast.

Shabana Azmi is absolutely remarkable as Mai. There is a quiet heartbreak in her performance, with every nuance carrying the weight of a woman who has lost almost everything but refuses to let go of the one thing she has left: hope. She commands attention whenever she appears on screen, making her casting one of the movie’s biggest strengths.
