title: Farah Khan tells Akanksha Choudhary that her daughters are insecure about their appearance: ‘They feel ugly’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Farah Khan was seen with Lock Upp 2 contestant Akanksha Choudhary in her latest YouTube vlog. What did Farah say? In the vlog, Farah asked Akanksha about her journey in the industry so far. Akanksha, who has participated in pageants before entering Splitsvilla, shared that she was not as confident before. She candidly shared, “Main toh mujhe sabse ugly lagti thi duniya mei (I used to find myself the ugliest in the entire world).” Akanksha then showed Farah her old pictures from her teenage years and shared she had been very insecure as a young girl. To this, Farah replied, “Please meet my daughters then! Even they feel that they are very ugly.” Akanksha shared that she has met them and they are very cute.

Adding to this, Akanksha then added that now she has become much more confident as a woman, even without makeup. Farah shared that she looked beautiful in Lock Upp while bare-faced. Farah also admitted that she was ‘horrified’ when Akanksha showed her other side on the show and threw water on Shreya Kalra 's bedsheet and picked an ugly fight with her.

Meanwhile, In May, Farah posted photos from the graduation ceremony at Dhirubhai Ambani International School in Mumbai as her children officially graduated. They will start their university studies this year.

Notably, Last year, in an episode of Two Much with Kajol and Twinkle , Farah spoke about how she had no movies and wasn’t directing, so she decided to try out YouTube. She also candidly admitted that sending three children to college is expensive, a challenge that her new career helps alleviate. “Even when my movie was not happening, when I wasn’t directing, I shared chal (come on), let me do YouTube. Also, I have 3 kids who will go to university next year, and that’s bloody expensive,” she shared, adding, “So I just shared for a change, let me start a show on YouTube, and that just clicked.”

title: Exclusive | Shreya Ghoshal to croon Mirzapur’s cult song Vaaroon with original singer Romy for film adaptation
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The followers of Mirzapur are in for a treat as one of the show’s most popular songs makes a comeback. The superhit, Vaaroon, which was integral to the first season, will be recreated for Mirzapur: The Movie . The song, titled Vaaroon Forever, will feature Shreya Ghoshal and Romy, the original singer.

Adding to this, Mirzapur’s Vaaroon gets a fresh musical spin with Shreya Ghoshal and Romy. Shreya Ghoshal joins the soundtrack The original Vaaroon was rolled out in 2020 and became popular due to its soulful Sufi music and lyrical lyrics. The music was composed by Anand Bhaskar, whereas the lyrics were written by Ginny Diwan. Both are back for the remixed version of the song that will be rolled out on Tuesday, August 18. Vaaroon was originally picturised on Ali Fazal and Shriya Pilgaonkar in the series.

Meanwhile, An independent source tells Hindustan Times, “The famous Vaaroon song from the Mirzapur franchise is set to be recreated for Mirzapur: The Movie, titled Vaaroon Forever. While the older version was sung by Romy, Shreya Ghoshal will be joining him on the mic this time.”

Notably, Mirzapur: The Movie will bring the popular franchise from the streaming platform to the theatre, reintroducing some of the characters that made the franchise a hit among its followers. This movie is being produced by Excel Entertainment and Amazon MGM Studios, with Farhan Akhtar and Ritesh Sidhwani as the producers.

As per the latest buzz, Gurmmeet Singh is making a return to direct the movie adaptation of Mirzapur, while the screenplay is being penned by Puneet Krishna. The theatrical adaptation is shared to keep the same gritty universe and the power dynamics that Mirzapur has always had but take the story into a bigger place. It will be set post the events of season 1.

In further updates, At the movie’s trailer launch, Farhan Akhtar spoke about how the audience played a key role in bringing the movie to life. He shared, “The show is a result of followers' love. They have supported the show from the time it was first rolled out. Amazon took it across the world. Wherever I used to go, people used to ask me, 'Ki Mirzapur kab aa rha hai?' When it was revealed, people used to ask me the rollout date, so it is really the followers that have demanded this movie. We are very happy and grateful to have put it together with the original cast and the amazing new cast.”

On top of that, The movie brings back some of the franchise’s most recognisable faces. Pankaj Tripathi returns as Kaleen Bhaiya, while Ali Fazal reprises his role as Guddu Pandit and Divyenndu returns as Munna Bhaiya. Ravi Kishan is also joining the story as a new antagonist who poses a fresh challenge to Kaleen Bhaiya’s hold over Mirzapur.

There is also a change in the casting of Bablu Pandit. Jitendra Kumar will now play the character, who was originally portrayed by Vikrant Massey in the series. Shweta Tripathi, Rasika Dugal, Shriya Pilgaonkar, Harshita Gaur, Sheeba Chaddha and Rajesh Tailang are also part of the ensemble.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Why Vinod Kambli’s life is being made as a series, not a Film; director Abhijeet Deshpande explains
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

With the V. Shantaram biopic pushed ahead, director Abhijeet Shirish Deshpande has shifted his focus to a new project. Speaking exclusively to Bollywood Hungama , Deshpande has opened up that he will next direct Kambli , a ZEE5 series based on the life of former Indian cricketer Vinod Kambli. The show will be produced by Ravi Bhagchandka’s 200NotOut Productions, the banner behind the acclaimed Sachin Tendulkar documentary Sachin: A Billion Dreams .

Adding to this, “I started writing Kambli in 2019. I began writing Kambli and V. Shantaram together. Ravi Bhagchandka, the producer, has been with me all throughout, and we are hoping to surprise people with our take on Kambli. It is a human story and not a sports movie,” reveals the director.

Meanwhile, Deshpande originally envisioned the project as a Marathi feature movie, but as he delved deeper into the former cricketer’s life, he realised that only a series format could do justice to his story. “When I studied his life, there was so much material and so much drama that it's impossible to encapsulate all of that in one movie. I think the series in Hindi will also help his story travel wider,” he explains.

Notably, The casting for the show has not been finalised yet, but the makers are looking for a fresh face who bears a close resemblance to Kambli. The aim is to treat the cricketer’s life and personality with sensitivity and realism. Shooting timelines have not been locked yet, but the makers are targeting a November 2026 start, with plans to complete the shoot in one go over three to four months. Deshpande will move on to V. Shantaram once this project is wrapped.

As per the latest buzz, Kambli will chronicle Vinod Kambli’s remarkable and turbulent journey from his early emergence as one of the country’s most promising young batting talents to the personal and professional challenges that altered the course of his career. It will trace a story beyond the headlines, exploring a life filled with immense promise, unforgettable achievements and personal struggles.

title: Ajay Devgn and Veena Devgn rent a 7,803 sq ft Juhu bungalow for Rs 16 lakh a month: Report
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Juhu is one of Mumbai’s most prestigious residential neighbourhoods, known for its upscale homes, star residences, and premium lifestyle offerings. Located along the western coastline, it combines a sought-after beachfront setting with strong connectivity to key business and commercial districts. The area has witnessed sustained demand for luxury residential properties, supported by established social infrastructure, retail, hospitality, and entertainment options. Limited availability of premium land and continued demand for high-end housing keep property values elevated across the micro-market.

Adding to this, According to property registration documents accessed by Square Yards, Ajay Devgn and his mother, Veena Devgn, have leased out a bungalow in Kapol CHS Ltd., Juhu. The rental agreement includes a security deposit of Rs. 48 lakh and was registered with a stamp duty of Rs. 2.71 lakh and registration charges of Rs. 1,000. The bungalow has a built-up area of 724.90 sq. m. (7,803 sq. ft.).

Meanwhile, As per Square Yards' analysis, the lease tenure spans 60 months (five years). The monthly rent starts at Rs. 16 lakh in the first year and escalates by 5% each year to approximately Rs. 19.45 lakh in the fifth year. Over the full term, the cumulative rental value is estimated at approximately Rs. 10.61 crore rupees.

title: Awarapan 2 box office collection day 1 (updated live): Emraan Hashmi film sails past part 1's lifetime haul in 9 hours
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Awarapan 2 ticket-window earnings day 1: Emraan Hashmi ’s Shivam Pandit has finally got his due at the ticket-window, it seems. Awarapan 2, the sequel, got off to a record-breaking start at the ticket window, poised to shatter records for Emraan Hashmi and Vishesh Films. It has also already surpassed the lifetime collection of Awarapan , the first part, before the end of day 1. Awarapan 2 is tracking to have one of the biggest openings for Bollywood in 2026 and has comfortably outpaced Batwara 1947, the Sunny Deol-starrer that clashed with it at the ticket-window on August 14.

Adding to this, Awarapan 2 ticket-window earnings day 1: Emraan Hashmi on the promotional poster of Awarapan 2. Awarapan 2 ticket-window update till 6 PM According to Sacnilk, Awarapan 2 has already collected over ₹ 12.05 crore rupees net by 6 pm on its rollout day. This makes the movie the highest-earning title in the fledgling franchise already. The first Awarapan, rolled out in 2007, was a ticket-window failure and collected only ₹ 7.76 crore rupees during its lifetime. Awarapan 2 took all of 8 hours to cross that mark.

Meanwhile, Awarapan 2 has been selling over 20k tickets per hour on BookMyShow all through Friday. This is a remarkable pace for any movie without a superstar. This means that it will cross not just ₹ 10 crore rupees but, in all likelihood, ₹ 20 crore rupees on its first day itself. This makes it the biggest opening of Emraan Hashmi’s career. So far, only two of Emraan’s films have had double-digit openings. Raaz 2 opened at ₹ 10.35 crore rupees in 2012. The record for Emraan was then broken by Baadshaho, which collected ₹ 12.60 crore rupees on its rollout day in 2017. Awarapan will easily leave both titles in the dust with its pace.
Notably, The first Awarapan had an opening-day collection of ₹ 79 lakh and netted ₹ 2.88 crore rupees in its first weekend. Even after accounting for inflation, this was a low figure.

As per the latest buzz, Directed by Nitin Kakkar and produced by Vishesh Bhatt, Awarapan 2 brings back Emraan Hashmi in his iconic role of Shivam Pandit. The movie also stars Shabana Azmi, Disha Patani , and Suvinder Vicky. The movie received mixed to positive reviews, but particular praise for Emraan Hashmi’s performance and the tone.

In further updates, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Movie Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera). With a good understanding of cinema and its trends, and a keen eye for detail, he continues to spark conversations around showbiz for readers around the world. Read More

title: Shekhar Kapur says Sridevi was almost in denial of her stardom, calls her director's best friend: ‘She was a gift’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Shekhar Kapur remembered late star Sridevi on her 63rd birth anniversary with a throwback picture taken when they worked together for the first time. He directed her in the 1987 science-fiction movie Mr India, which is often considered one of the best films in her iconic career.

Adding to this, Shekhar Kapur penned a heartfelt note for Sridevi on her birth anniversary. Sridevi, who died in 2018 aged 54, began her career as a child star and went on to become one of the most celebrated female stars in Indian cinema, working across Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam films.

Meanwhile, Shekhar wrote a long note in the caption of his Instagram post to remember the star. He shared, “The earliest pic I have of Sridevi and myself. Her face never changed. Her eyes flashed startlingly in this pic from the movie ‘Joshilay’ as much as they did later in ‘Mr India’ .. and while the world remembers the Star .. Sridevi .. on her birth yesterday I was remembering Sri Devi as the Director’s best friend.”

Notably, “Mr India would not have been possible without the amazing collaboration between Sridevi and myself. I still remember my excitement and urge to get to the set when Sri Devi and I were doing Mr India ..because you never knew how Sri Devi would surprise you that day. .. and she never failed to do so,” he added.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shekhar kapur (@shekharkapur)

In further updates, Shekhar recalled, “When the camera was not in her .. she would be quietly sitting in her chair .. almost in denial of her stardom (unlike actors today she would not disappear into her trailer). When in front of the Camera it was as if magic happened .. it was a different Sridevi.. her energy not only radiated out of her for the camera .. everyone on the set felt it .. it was electric. So much that at times ( especially in a dance sequence) we would forget to switch off the camera ! For I would forget to say ‘Cut’ .. I doubt there’ll be another Sri Devi .. she was a gift to us ..So wherever you are Sri .. Happy Birthday.”

On top of that, Born as Shree Amma Yanger Ayyapan in 1963, Sridevi was known for her iconic roles in Hindi movies such as Chandni, Lamhe, Mr India, Chaalbaaz, Nagina, Sadma, and English Vinglish, among many more. The Padma Shri awardee had also made a mark with her performances in Tamil, Telugu, Hindi, Malayalam, and Kannada films. Her last movie was Mom, for which she also received the Best Star National Award, posthumously.

Sridevi died in Dubai at the age of 54 on February 24, 2018 in a Dubai hotel bathroom. The autopsy report called it an 'accidental drowning' in the bathtub. She was in the United Arab Emirates for the wedding of star-nephew Mohit Marwah.

title: Jharkhand protest: 300 unnamed rioters booked for assault, vandalism in Ranchi
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Jharkhand police has registered a first information report (FIR) against unknown individuals at the Vidhan Sabha police station in connection with the August 10 march by job aspirants to the state assembly over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in the state, people aware of the development shared on Thursday.

Adding to this, Ranchi: Security personnel stand guard as people march towards Jharkhand Assembly amid a protest over alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC examination, JSSC-CGL and other recruitment tests. (PTI) Talking to HT, a police officer familiar with the matter shared the FIR was registered on Wednesday based on the statement of the magistrate on duty, Mohammed Nishat Ahmad. “The police have filed an FIR against unidentified rioters under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. Charges have been framed under Sections 109, 115(2), 117(2), 121, 132, 189(2)(3), 190, 191(2), 221, 223, 285 and 352 for obstructing government work, assaulting public servants and damaging public property. Sub-Inspector (SI) Anand Pandit has been assigned to investigate the case. The police are currently analysing video footage and photographs to identify the perpetrators,” the officer shared.

Meanwhile, A copy of the FIR available with HT does not mention the number of alleged rioters. Ranchi superintendent of police (city) Paras Rana, however, told a news agency that the case had been filed against "300 unknown" people.

Notably, According to the FIR, the protest march towards the Jharkhand assembly turned violent when miscreants, allegedly operating under the guise of a student movement, clashed with security forces.
As per the latest buzz, The mob damaged public property and attacked police personnel and magistrates on duty. Several police officers sustained serious injuries during the clash.

In further updates, The FIR shared a large crowd of students moving from the old assembly route towards the new Vidhan Sabha building forcibly broke through the initial defensive drop-gates and barricades erected by the administration, reaching near Niladri Bhavan by 12.15 pm.

On top of that, The on-duty magistrate, a revenue sub-inspector of Nagri Circle, used a public-address system to pacify the crowd, reminding them that section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was in force because the assembly session was underway. Ignoring the warnings, the miscreants in the crowd clashed with police and uprooted barricades near Yogoda Satsang. The situation quickly escalated, with the mob allegedly pelting magistrates and police personnel with slippers, shoes, water bottles and stones.

Several police officers were hurt in the stone-pelting with trainee constable Falguni Yadav sustaining head injuries and was rushed to hospital along with other injured personnel for immediate medical treatment. Students’ spokesperson Piyush Kumar Singh shared the FIR should not be used to harass genuine students. “No genuine student should be harassed,” he shared.

title: How sensitive retelling of Partition found place in Bollywood's azaadi stories; Imtiaz Ali and Rajkumar Santoshi explain
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In two months, Hindi cinema has seen the rollout of two big films set during the Partition of India. Mind you, I use the term Partition, not Independence, because these two films make that distinction clearly. Both Main Vaapas Aaunga and Batwara 1947 talk about the human cost of the Partition of India and Pakistan, but without talking about the hatred or vitriol. These are films about love, about hope, and most importantly, about learning from the past. Two films may not signify a trend, but 2026 has shown that Bollywood can speak sensitively about something as painful as the Partition.

Adding to this, Vedang Raina plays a young Sikh man forced to leave his village after Partition in Main Vaapas Aaunga. ‘A story of two people but also of a country’ Imtiaz Ali ’s Main Vaapas Aaunga is a love story that transcends time and borders. Set in 1947, it is about Keenu (Vedang Raina) and Jiya (Sharvari) living on, keeping the promise to each other in their hearts. “This is a story of two people but also the story of a country,” the filmmaker tells us. Imtiaz says he understood the challenge of making a soft love story set during the biggest humanitarian tragedy in history. But he found the middle ground by ‘focusing on Jiya and Keenu’. He explains, “It is their personal story and everything else that is happening is kind of out of focus.”

Meanwhile, It’s not as if stories of Partition have not been told in Hindi films before. But they have been about pain (like Pinjar) or rage (in Gadar). The shift now is that films talk about moving past that pain, towards hope, redemption, and moving forward. Batwara 1947, directed by Rajkumar Santoshi, is massier than Main Vaapas Aunga, but retains the humanity of the stories around Partition. The movie stars Sunny Deol as a Muslim man who moves to Pakistan during Partition, only to find a Hindu woman, played by Shabana Azmi, still living in his new home. As tensions rise, he takes responsibility for protecting her while keeping his family safe.

Notably, Talking about taking an objective approach to telling a story from that era, director Santoshi says, “Partition ke time pe yeh dekha gaya hai insaan ne bulandiyan bhi touch ki hai, great courage dikhaya hai, great sacrifices bhi diye hain, aur utne ghinaune harkat bhi insaan ne kiye hain. Yeh donon cheez Partition mein dekhi gayi hain. Iss movie mein bhi aise emotions hain. (It has been observed that during the Partition, humanity scaled great heights—demonstrating immense courage and making profound sacrifices—yet also committed truly heinous acts. Both these facets were witnessed during the Partition. This movie captures those very emotions).”

As per the latest buzz, Both these films have one commonality with other stories about Partition. They look at it through the lens of an individual or a family, rather than as a nation, thereby personalising pain. But while earlier, the pain was largely about the loss of home or identity, now it has transcended that. Preity Zinta , who returns to the big screen with Batwara 1947, explains, “It’s not about ki udhar kya ho raha hai, idhar kya ho raha hai (what is happening this side or that side). It’s about humare ghar mein kya ho raha hai (what is happening in my home). When world events happen, you don’t look at it that way. Woh toh history mein in retrospect aap dekh ke bolte hain ki arre aisa hua (You look back and reflect on how it happened). When you are going through a situation, your first instinct is: my family and me. That is how different people react.”

In further updates, The challenge to that is not reducing the political upheaval and the human tragedy to something subservient to an individual’s ‘selfish’ pain. But Imtiaz says a balance has to be sought. “It's not as though that we are pretending that it is not happening. We are not trying to say that what is happening is pleasant at all. We fully respect and acknowledge the authenticity of the incidents that occurred in 1947. However, the story is about a young boy and a young girl who are deeply aggrieved by the events of Partition for a very personal reason. They are not so mature or large-hearted as to say that the division of the country is my problem. For them, the problem is the divide between you and me. That's what matters to people personally,” says the filmmaker.

On top of that, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Movie Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera). With a good understanding of cinema and its trends, and a keen eye for detail, he continues to spark conversations around showbiz for readers around the world. Read More

title: Awarapan 2 first reactions: Emraan Hashmi wins roaring response as Shivam Pandit, fans call sequel a ‘smash hit’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

After years of anticipation, Emraan Hashmi is back as Shivam Pandit, and the first reactions to Awarapan 2 suggest that the character has lost none of his impact. The sequel to the 2007 cult favourite arrived in theatres worldwide on August 14, bringing back the brooding and intense protagonist while taking his story in a new direction. Directed by Nitin Kakkar and backed by Vishesh Films, Awarapan 2 also stars Disha Patani and Shabana Azmi . This time, Shivam finds himself caught between redemption, love and the dangerous criminal world once again, with his relationship with a child becoming a key part of the emotional story.

Adding to this, Awarapan 2 Twitter Review: Followers go wild for Emraan Hashmi’s return, call sequel a ‘definitive smash hit’. First reactions to Awarapan 2 Trade analyst Taran Adarsh was among those who shared an early verdict on the movie, praising both Hashmi's return and the sequel's nostalgic appeal. He wrote, "#OneWordReview... #Awarapan2: SMASH-HIT. Rating: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐ #EmraanHashmi returns as #ShivamPandit, and what a return it is... He is the SOUL of #Awarapan2... Mass-appealing moments + tremendous nostalgia value... SURE-SHOT SUCCESS."

Meanwhile, He highlighted the emotional core of the sequel, particularly Shivam's bond with the child, while appreciating the way the movie mixes drama with action. He noted, "What stands out most about #Awarapan2 is Shivam's story – this time, his bond with a child takes centre stage... The narrative takes a completely different path, with action pieces generously sprinkled across the proceedings." He further lauded Hashmi's performance, saying, “brings vulnerability, intensity, and a lived-in quality to the character, making Shivam's journey deeply affecting... This is one of the most compelling performances of his filmography.”

Notably, The early response from other viewers has also been strongly positive. One critic described the sequel as a tightly packed thriller that maintains the gritty feel of the original while giving it a bigger and more contemporary treatment. The user wrote, “#Awarapan2 is a relentlessly gripping, tight-rope thriller that grabs you by the throat from its opening sequence and refuses to let go! ... Awarapan2 is a non-stop, high-octane entertainment marathon! It captures the raw, gritty charm of the original cult classic while injecting an incredible amount of new-age scale, energy, and suspenseful writing. A definitive smash hit!”

As per the latest buzz, Another reaction on X (formerly Twitter) focused on the darker mood of the sequel and Hashmi's performance, stating, “#Awarapan2 is a moody, emotional noir sequel that brilliantly honors its classic predecessor. Driven by a powerful, rage-filled performance from #EmraanHashmi, the movie delivers stylized, poetic, and violent direction. - Emraan Hashmi is back.”

In further updates, Followers, meanwhile, appear particularly excited to see Hashmi step back into one of his most remembered characters. One fan wrote on X, “Awarapan 2: It's all about #EmraanHashmi. He doesn't need to do anything extra. He simply lives his life with a new purpose. That intensity, that charisma, Shivam is still Shivam.”

On top of that, Another viewer lauded the movie for balancing its emotional moments with the larger-than-life treatment, writing, “#Awarapan2: Smash hit! Emraan Hashmi owns it as Shivam Pandit. Massy, emotional, nostalgic & powerful. Outstanding performance + Soulful music. Disha patani good work. Shabana Azmi superb.”

The second part of Awarapan kicks off with Shivam Pandit who is still haunted by the loss of Aaliyah from the first movie. His life takes another unexpected turn when he gets an opportunity to save a baby girl's life. This looks like an opportunity to get rid of his guilt until it leads him into the dangerous world of child trafficking. He goes to Bangkok where he is supposed to hunt down the person responsible for this whole scam. Thus, this movie differs from its predecessor as the protagonist of the first movie embarks on yet another struggle but this time he is emotionally scarred.

title: Awarapan 2 review: Brooding Emraan Hashmi brings back the 2000s with a nostalgic sequel
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

It’s been 19 years since the first Awarapan , a movie that bombed at the ticket-window upon rollout. But there’s no business like movie business. Today, thanks to the cult following the original developed organically over the years, Awarapan 2 has opened to packed houses, and my show was no different.

Adding to this, Sitting in the theatre, I was transported back to the 2000s, when Vishesh Films had a knack for churning out films at a rapid pace. Murder, Zeher, Gangster, to name a few. They shared a peculiar similarity: most were crime thrillers that worked, starred Emraan Hashmi in the lead, and came with songs that had a shelf life far longer than their theatrical runs. Awarapan 2 follows much of the same template, and for the most part, it works.

Meanwhile, The story picks up from where Awarapan left off. Shivam (Emraan Hashmi) has survived the six bullets pumped into his body in the last scene of the first movie. Away from the murky underworld now, he becomes attached to a baby he rescues. He names her Aliyah (Myrah Shivan), after his now-dead sweetheart. However, soon after Aliyah is adopted, Interpol informs him that she was, in fact, being pushed into the child trafficking business. Shivam sets out to save her, but to do so, he needs to earn the trust of Zorawar (Puran Gabbi) and find a place within his gang, which runs the trafficking operation. What follows forms the crux of the plot.

Notably, Writer Bilal Siddiqui cracks a decent, if predictable, plot that will certainly remind viewers of a bygone era. Thankfully, the production values don’t belong to the bygone era. Shot in Bangkok, money has been spent on creating real environments rather than relying entirely on AI or VFX-rendered backdrops.

As per the latest buzz, The first half of this Nitin Kakkar directorial is effective in keeping the viewer hooked, with the rehash of the popular Toh Phir Aao doing much of the heavy lifting on the nostalgia front. There are stretches, though, where the story begins to test your patience and feels repetitive. There’s a gunfight every 15-20 minutes, which means the characters barely have time to process one shootout before another one arrives. After a point, even the bullets seem to be working overtime.
In further updates, The second half gets much of the same treatment, with Tera Mera Rishta taking over the nostalgia duties. The climax, thankfully, works and should land well with viewers.

On top of that, Performance-wise, this is the quintessential Emraan Hashmi an entire generation grew up watching. He hasn’t aged a day since Awarapan rolled out. He delivers exactly what is expected of him: brooding intensity, and the kind of effortless cool that made him a star in the first place.

Shabana Azmi is the next scene-stealer. She exudes power the moment she enters the frame as Nafisa, the gangster queen, commanding attention without having to do much. At this point, Awarapan 3 should probably be about her backstory.

title: Aaradhya Bachchan case: Delhi HC asks if Bachchan family name's reputation 'flows down generationally'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In 2023, Aaradhya Bachchan , daughter of Abhishek Bachchan and Aishwarya Rai , filed a case in the Delhi High Court alleging that "absolutely false" videos about her health and private life had been published on YouTube. A plea was filed seeking protection of her personality rights. On Thursday, the Delhi High Court raised several key legal questions that it will consider while hearing Aaradhya's case.

Adding to this, Abhishek Bachchan, Aaradhya Bachchan and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan What Delhi High Court shared in Aaradhya Bachchan's case The case was initiated after multiple YouTube videos made baseless allegations about her health, including claims that she was seriously ill and had been hospitalised. During Thursday's hearing, Justice Anup J Bhambhani observed that the value and reputation of a trademark were attached to a product or service, but the case was "somewhat contextually different when you are talking about a person."

Meanwhile, Justice Bhambhani asked, "If a family name is akin to having a reputation attached to a trademark, how far down the generations does such reputation of family name inure? A certain last name has a reputation because of the achievements, the eminence in a certain field of work, etc. So, does that reputation, that you are couching as virtually as a trademark … Does that flow down generationally? If so, up to what point?"

Notably, The court also questioned whether publishing fake or misleading news, even if it is of an “egregiously despicable nature”, could constitute a violation of intellectual property rights and, if so, which type of IP right may have been infringed. Advocate Pravin Anand, representing the plaintiffs, argued that any attempt to damage or exploit the family's goodwill must be stopped, noting that such goodwill could diminish over time. The lawyer also pointed out that pictures of the entire family were being used and that the Bachchan name was being associated with the alleged fake news.

As per the latest buzz, The court had previously, on April 20, 2023, restrained several YouTube channels from sharing misleading content about Aaradhya Bachchan's health. The single-judge bench observed that spreading misinformation about a child reflected “morbid perversity” and shared Google could not allow such content to be disseminated.

In further updates, The court had further stressed that every child has the right to be treated with honour and respect, adding that spreading misleading information about a child's health was “completely intolerable in law”. The matter is now scheduled to be heard next in September.

On top of that, Aaradhya, represented by her father Abhishek Bachchan, approached the Delhi High Court in 2023 against several YouTube channels and unidentified individuals over allegedly defamatory and misleading content about her and the Bachchan family. The case involved videos falsely claiming that she was seriously ill and hospitalised, with one even alleging her death, while others accused the family of delaying her medical treatment. The plea also sought protection of their private information. With inputs from PTI

title: Ajay Devgn rents out Mumbai’s Juhu bungalow for ₹16 lakh a month; to earn an estimated ₹10.61 crore over 5 years
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Bollywood star Ajay Devgn and his mother, Veena Devgn, have leased out their 7,802.75 sq ft bungalow in Mumbai’s Juhu for five years, with the total rent estimated at ₹ 10.61 crore rupees, according to property registration documents accessed by Zapkey.

Adding to this, Bollywood star Ajay Devgn has leased out his 7,802.75 sq ft bungalow in Mumbai’s Juhu for five years, with the total rent estimated at ₹10.61 crore rupees, documents accessed by Zapkey showed. The leave and licence agreement was registered on August 10, 2026. The bungalow, located at Kapole CHS Ltd, N S Road No. 11, JVPD Scheme, opposite Daftary Nursing Home in Juhu, Mumbai, has been leased to Florian Hurel Salons Private Limited.

Meanwhile, The property has a built-up area of 724.90 sq m (7,802.75 sq ft). The monthly rent is ₹ 16 lakh in the first year, increasing by 5% annually. The rent will rise to ₹ 16.8 lakh in the second year, ₹ 17.64 lakh in the third year, ₹ 18.52 lakh in the fourth year and ₹ 19.45 lakh in the fifth year, the documents showed.

Notably, The agreement includes a security deposit of ₹ 48 lakh. The stamp duty paid on the transaction was ₹ 2.71 lakh, while the registration charges stood at ₹ 1,000, the lease and license documents showed.

As per the latest buzz, Ajay Devgn, also known as Vishal Veery Devgn and Veena Devgn are listed as the lessors, with Mohnish Shashikant Dhavale acting through a power of attorney. Florian Hurel Salons Private Limited is the lessee, represented by its authorised signatory Zarir Furshostre Meherji.

In further updates, In 2021, Ajay Devgn had taken a loan against the property. He had purchased the bungalow for ₹ 47.5 crore rupees and had taken a loan of ₹ 18.75 crore rupees, according to earlier media reports citing Zapkey.com. The bungalow was purchased on December 29, 2020, while the loan was taken on April 27, 2021, the documents showed.
On top of that, The star paid ₹ 2.37 crore rupees in stamp duty on the transaction. The documents indicated that the property was transferred through a transfer deed rather than a sale deed.

According to Square Yards, Juhu is one of Mumbai’s most prestigious residential neighbourhoods, known for its luxury homes , star residences and premium lifestyle offerings. The coastal neighbourhood also offers strong connectivity to key business and commercial districts, along with established social infrastructure, retail, hospitality and entertainment options. Limited availability of premium land and sustained demand for high-end housing have kept property values elevated in the micro-market.

The screenwriter made his directorial debut with the espionage thriller series Saare Jahan Se Accha and has also directed the satirical comedy-drama Baaghi Bechare, starring Pratik Gandhi, Abhishek Banerjee and Faisal Malik, which is yet to be rolled out. title: 'Between me and students': CJI Surya Kant slams Bar Council move against protesters
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Friday came down heavily on the Bar Council of India (BCI) over its intervention in the NALSAR University of Law enrolment row, saying the Council had “no business” interfering with students’ right to protest and making it clear that the court would not allow students to be stopped from raising their voice through lawful and peaceful protests. He restrained the BCI and all state bar councils from pursuing any punitive or criminal action against students and faculty of any national law university or university in connection with the row.

Adding to this, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant shared, "It's a dialogue between the students and me." (PTI) The CJI’s observations came hours after BCI chairman Manan Kumar Mishra opened up that the Council had decided to close its proceedings against the 2026 graduating batch of NALSAR, Hyderabad, after initially freezing their enrolment and then withdrawing the freeze while retaining an inquiry into those allegedly instrumental in the students’ campaign against CJI Kant being invited as chief guest at their convocation.

Meanwhile, The Supreme Court , meanwhile, took on board a petition seeking directions to restrain the BCI from issuing such directives in future and issued notice to the Council. A bench headed by CJI Kant, along with justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, directed the BCI to file its counter-affidavit within two weeks.

Notably, “The BCI is unnecessarily taking action in this matter. If students have a cause or a reason to protest, they have a right to protest. Nobody can stop them, and we will not allow this,” shared the CJI after senior advocate K Parameshwar mentioned the matter before the bench.

As per the latest buzz, Parameshwar submitted that the BCI had “no business” dealing with what was happening inside a university and that its action violated the students’ fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression. He shared the BCI’s withdrawal of the first letter freezing enrolment did not wipe out the cause of action against the Council. “It spells a lot about the functioning of the BCI,” Parameshwar shared.

In further updates, The CJI responded: “We are with you. This is absolutely uncalled for. They had no business to interfere. The students have written a letter to me, and it is between me and the students. There is a dialogue between us.”

On top of that, The Chief Justice also drew upon his own experience as a student to underscore the importance of allowing dissent on university campuses. “In my younger days, I was also actively involved in student activities. They have a right to protest. Who can stop them? So long as they are lawfully and peacefully protesting, they have a right to raise their voice,” he shared.
At another point, the CJI shared: “We have to be large-hearted. They should be allowed to speak. Even if they are wrong, they have a right to speak.”

Toh ek message nahi de raha hoon main. Teacher thode hi hoon (I am not giving a message, I am not a teacher). The movie should be good, and people should enjoy it,” he shared.

On top of that, Filmmaker Ramesh Taurani watched Batwara 1947 at a special screening on Wednesday and wrote on Instagram, “Batwara 1947 is a deeply sensitive, moving and truly humanity-glorifying movie that deserves to be watched First Day, First Show. It is a powerful reminder of the resilience of the human spirit and the importance of compassion, especially during the darkest chapters of our history. @iamsunnydeol delivers a terrific and deeply impactful performance. title: Kitu Gidwani calls Bollywood ‘fake industry’, slams its vague rules: ‘I should have been able to live off royalties’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Kitu Gidwani has spent over four decades in the entertainment industry, working across films and television and building a career that includes memorable projects such as Jaane Tu Ya Jaane Na , Fashion and Dhobi Ghat, as well as iconic TV shows like Shaktimaan and Swabhimaan. Now, the veteran star has opened up about some of her biggest frustrations with Bollywood, calling the industry "fake" and questioning its treatment of artistes, particularly older women. In a recent interview with Screen, Kitu also criticised the lack of royalties for artistes and the limited, stereotypical roles offered to women as they age.

Adding to this, Kitu Gidwani slams lack of powerful roles for women in Bollywood. Kitu Gidwani slams Bollywood Talking about how several musicians have been fighting for unpaid royalties, Kitu shared actors face the same issue. She shared, "Bollywood is not a real industry; it’s a cottage industry. It’s a fake industry; it goes by its own vague rules. There is nothing like Hollywood’s Screen Actors Guild in India. I should have been able to work for 10 years and then live off my royalties for the next ten years, not slog for 40 years. Intellectual property rights and creative rights are zero in India."

Meanwhile, She further criticised the lack of rights actors have over their work, pointing out that producers typically pay actors and directors a one-time fee and then retain complete ownership and control over the property. She added, "It’s not like that anywhere in the world. My grouse against the industry is that older women are not getting powerful roles. We don’t want to play the generic mother or maasi. We want to play good, enduring roles with sex, love, power, comedy, and action. In daily soaps, once a woman hits 30, she becomes a daadi. She has no signs of aging on her face, but she gets such roles. This industry is very bizarre.”

Notably, In Hollywood, actors are represented by unions such as SAG-AFTRA, while writers and directors have the WGA and DGA, respectively. These unions have negotiated provisions that can provide performers and writers with additional payments when films, television shows or other content are reused, syndicated, licensed or made available on certain platforms. These payments are often referred to as residuals.

As per the latest buzz, Kitu began her acting journey in 1984 with the movie Holi, which also featured Aamir Khan, Ashutosh Gowariker, Om Puri and others. She gained popularity after starring in the TV series Air Hostess, which aired on Doordarshan in 1986. She then played Svetlana in Swabhimaan, which made her a household name. She later joined Shaktimaan, playing Geeta Vishwas, a news reporter who stood for the truth. However, she left the show after a few episodes.

In further updates, Apart from television, Kitu has also received critical acclaim for her performances in films such as Dance of the Wind (1997), Deepa Mehta's Earth (1998), Govind Nihalani's Rukhmavati Ki Haveli (1991), Kamal Haasan's Abhay and Deham (2001).

title: Rani Mukerji honoured for 3 decades in cinema: ‘My films, my characters and my voice have travelled so far from home’

Rani Mukerji celebrates 3 decades of roles Rani attended the festival in a striking geranium-red monochrome co-ord set as she marked the latest recognition in an already celebrated career. From playing women who went against social expectations to portraying characters who found courage during difficult times, the star has consistently brought honesty and emotional depth to her performances.

Meanwhile, Her filmography includes a wide range of roles, with films such as Black, Hum Tum, Yuva, Bunty Aur Babli, No One Killed Jessica, Hichki, the Mardaani franchise and Mrs. Chatterjee vs Norway showcasing different sides of her acting.

Notably, Speaking about the honour, Rani Mukerji shared, “When I entered the Indian movie industry as a young girl, I never imagined that one day my films and the characters that I have been fortunate enough to play would take me across oceans, and that people in a beautiful country like Australia would embrace me with so much warmth. Entertaining people across the world through my cinema is the greatest gift this profession has given me. Australia has always welcomed me and Indian cinema with open arms. It has become a place where cultures meet through storytelling, where films remind us that emotions don't need passports, and where love, laughter and hope speak a language we all understand.”

As per the latest buzz, She also reflected on how her characters have shaped her personally over the years. Rani added, “As actors, we perform in front of a camera. But the real story begins only when that performance reaches someone's heart. To know that for three decades my films, my characters and my voice have travelled so far from home and still found a place in your lives is incredibly humbling. I've been fortunate to play women who laughed loudly, loved deeply, fought fearlessly and never stopped believing in themselves. In many ways, every character has changed me a little. They've made me a better star, but more importantly, they've made me a better human being.”

In further updates, Rani's recognition also highlights the growing international reach of Indian cinema and her long-standing connection with audiences outside India. Her work has travelled well beyond the traditional Hindi movie audience, with several of her performances continuing to resonate with viewers across different cultures.
On top of that, The 2026 edition of IFFM is being held from August 13 to 23 and brings together films, actors and filmmakers from across India.

title: Sunny Deol recreates 'papa hu papa' from Oggy and the Cockroaches to perfection, internet can't believe the crossover
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Sunny Deol has been busy promoting his new movie, Batwara 1947. For the same, the veteran star undertook a massive nationwide city tour along with the movie’s cast and director Rajkumar Santoshi . One of the final stops in the tour was Kolkata, where he interacted with followers at an event. But apart from some Batwara talks, Sunny stunned followers with a rather unbelievable crossover. The star obliged a fan, recreating a dialogue from the animated show Oggy and the Cockroaches, which was dubbed in ‘his voice’ originally.

Adding to this, Sunny Deol channeled his inner Jack during the movie promotion of Batwara 1947, in Kolkata on Wednesday. (ANI Photo) Sunny Deol’s Oggy and the Cockroaches shoutout In videos shared from the stage at the Kolkata event for Batwara 1947, Sunny addresses a large, packed auditorium when a fan asks him to say a line. Explaining the context, the fan tells the star about Oggy and the Cockroaches. “There is a line in it in your voice, sir, where the character says, ‘Oye main papa hoon, duniya ka papa (I am the daddy, world’s daddy). Please can you say that in your style.”

Meanwhile, Sunny first smiles at the request and says, “I haven’t watched it, but you are saying he says, ‘main papa hoon, duniya ka papa’. So let me try.” The star then recreated the line in Hindi and Punjabi in his signature bold style to loud cheers from the crowd.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Samagya (@samagya_entertainment)

As per the latest buzz, The video of Sunny giving Oggy and the Cockroaches a shoutout in this manner went widely shared on Instagram in no time. Many comments expressed disbelief. “Now I can die peacefully,” chirped one. Another shared, “We got Sunny paaji saying Jack’s line before GTA VI.” Others took it further and joked that this style would look funny for Sunny’s next character. The star plays Lord Hanuman in Ramayana. “Imagine him saying to Ravana-Oye utha utha k patkunga tod dunga fod dunga oye..main papa hun iss Lanka ka Papa,” joked one social media user.

In further updates, Oggy and the Cockroaches was an animated series created in Canada by Jean-Yves Raimbaud and produced by Gaumont Multimedia. It aired from 1998 to 2019 across seven seasons. It began airing on Nickelodeon in India in 2009. In 2012, it was acquired by Cartoon Network for India, acquiring Bollywood-style voiceovers, with Jack, a green cat, voiced in the style of Sunny Deol. The series and its voice acting proved extremely popular in India, making the show part of the country's pop culture.

On top of that, Helmed by Rajkumar Santoshi, the movie stars Sunny Deol as a Muslim man who moves to Pakistan during Partition, only to find a Hindu woman, played by Shabana Azmi, still living in his new home. As tensions rise, he takes responsibility for protecting her while keeping his family safe. The movie also stars Preity Zinta, Karan Deol, Ali Fazal, Abhimanyu Singh, Khushi Hajare, and Kanikka Kapur. Backed by Aamir Khan Productions, the movie has rolled out in theatres today (August 14).

title: Pooja Bedi says she won't marry fiancé Maneck Contractor despite 8-year engagement: 'I've been there, done that'
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Star Pooja Bedi has opened up about her decision not to marry her fiancé Maneck Contractor , despite the couple having been engaged for eight years. In a recent conversation with Vickey Lalwani on his YouTube channel, Pooja explained how her views on marriage have changed over the years and why she no longer sees the need to formalise their relationship.

Adding to this, Pooja Bedi is engaged to Maneck Contractor. Pooja Bedi reveals why she doesn't want to get married Pooja opened up that while she once strongly believed in the institution of marriage, her views have evolved over the years. She shared that she is currently in a relationship with Maneck and that they have been engaged for eight years. While people often ask them when they plan to get married, she reminds them that they are not getting married.

Meanwhile, Explaining her decision not to marry, Pooja shared, "Engagement is when a person puts a ring on your finger and says, 'I want to be married to you.' Which basically says, I want to spend the rest of my life with you by my side, as a companion, as your lover, as your husband, and as a father of your children. The commitment is enough. After the commitment is there, all you're really doing is signing a piece of paper and getting the government involved in your affair.”

Notably, "It is so much easier. I've been married, I've been divorced, and I have two children. He's been married, he's been divorced, and he has kids too. In terms of simple things, like in terms of your assets, it's so simple. My assets go to my kids; his assets go to his kids. I'm earning, he's earning, and we're both independent. I don't need him for security's sake. He doesn't need me for financial security,” she added.

As per the latest buzz, Pooja shared that while the intention was initially to get married, the reality of what marriage looked like for them did not align with their vision for life. She explained that she does not want to be "contracted to somebody", adding that she has "been there, done that". She shared she believes everyone should get married and considers marriage a wonderful space, but does not personally feel the need to do it again.

In further updates, Pooja Bedi is the daughter of star Kabir Bedi and the late classical dancer Protima Bedi. She married businessman Farhan Furniturewala in 1994 and stepped away from films after marriage. The couple welcomed two children, daughter Alaya F and son Omar, before ending their marriage in 2003. Bedi has maintained a cordial relationship with Farhan, who is now married to Laila Khan Furniturewala.

On top of that, A few years after her divorce, Pooja reconnected with Maneck, who had been her senior at The Lawrence School, Sanawar, through their alumni WhatsApp group. In 2019, he proposed to her atop a hot-air balloon. Announcing her engagement, she tweeted, “He has literally swept me off my feet... i accepted Maneck Contractor’s proposal whilst sailing in a hot air balloon. Wish all of you a lifetime of happiness & to always dream of a rainbow at the end of a storm.”

Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Maddock Films (@maddockfilms)

As per the latest buzz, The official teaser of Prahaar was rolled out in June, offering the first glimpse of Rajkummar Rao in a powerful transformation as celebrated Indian public prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam . The teaser introduces viewers to a tense and investigative world, built around a wall covered with case files, photographs and notes linked to "Terror in Mumbai: City Under Siege."

In further updates, The visuals focus on the pursuit of truth and justice, while highlighting the long-awaited resolution surrounding the hanging of Ajmal Kasab. Rajkummar Rao steps into the role of Nikam, the prosecutor known for handling several high-profile cases.

title: Cocktail 2 OTT release: When and where to watch Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, Rashmika Mandanna's ₹147 crore hit
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Almost two months after its theatrical rollout, romantic drama Cocktail 2, starring Shahid Kapoor , Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna , is set to rollout on streaming. The movie received criticism upon rollout but was eventually a box-office success.

Adding to this, Cocktail 2 OTT rollout: Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, Rashmika movie is now out on streaming. Cocktail 2 OTT rollout Starting Friday, August 14, Cocktail 2 will begin streaming on Netflix. Sharing the update on social media, a post on the streaming giant's account read, “Two's a couple, and three's a Cocktail You've got a date Watch Cocktail 2, out 14 August on Netflix .” This was accompanied by a poster of the movie.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Netflix India (@netflix_in)

Notably, Directed by Homi Adjania, Cocktail 2 follows Shahid Kapoor and Rashmika Mandanna, a young couple deeply in love but unsure about marriage. Their vacation in Sicily takes an unexpected turn when they meet Diya's friend Ally, played by Kriti Sanon . What begins as a carefree trip soon turns into an emotional test of trust, love, and commitment.

As per the latest buzz, Cocktail 2 rolled out in theatres on June 19, 2026 to largely negative reviews. On the review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, only 23% of the movie's reviews are positive. It has a weighted rating of 5 out of 10 on the platform. Cocktail 2 was criticised for its lack of depth, slow pace, and not enough layers in the female characters. The HT review of the movie read: “This spiritual successor has the gloss, the glamour, but not the emotional punch. Some drinks are best served once.”

In further updates, Despite this, the movie was a big box-office success. The movie opened at ₹ 13 crore rupees net in India and sprinted to ₹ 47 crore rupees domestically in its opening weekend. Even as word of mouth did not pick up as expected, Cocktail 2 was able to cross ₹ 100 crore rupees domestically, on top of $3.7 million overseas. By the end of its run in theatres last week, Cocktail 2 had collected ₹ 147 crore rupees worldwide. As of August 14, it is the 6th-highest-grossing Hindi movie of the year.

On top of that, Cocktail 2 is the spiritual successor to director Homi Adajania's Cocktail, a critical and commercial success rolled out in 2012. The original movie starred Deepika Padukone, Saif Ali Khan, and Diana Penty.

title: Batwara 1947 and Awarapan 2 Movie Review, Release Live Updates
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

SUMMARY Emraan Hashmi returns to one of his most recognisable characters with 'Awarapan 2', which hits theatres today, almost two decades after the first movie. Directed by Nitin Kakkar, the sequel brings back Hashmi as Shivam, with Disha Patani and Shabana Azmi joining him in key roles. The biggest advantage for the movie is undoubtedly the emotional connect that the 2007 original has developed over the years. While 'Awarapan' did not emerge as a major theatrical success upon rollout, its music, intense romantic drama and Hashmi's portrayal of a troubled gangster gradually collected it a loyal cult following. The sequel appears to be consciously tapping into that sentiment, bringing back the character and the world that followers have remained attached to. The music is another major nostalgia factor, with the soundtrack carrying the musical identity associated with the franchise and a reprise of the much-loved 'Toh Phir Aao' adding to the recall value. For Hashmi, who has experienced several ups and downs at the ticket-window in recent years, the movie could provide a much-needed commercial breakthrough. A strong opening combined with positive word of mouth could make 'Awarapan 2' one of his most significant successes in a long time. Running alongside it is Sunny Deol's 'Batwara 1947', a period drama directed by Rajkumar Santoshi and produced by Aamir Khan. The movie features an ensemble cast comprising Deol, Preity Zinta, Shabana Azmi, Karan Deol, Ali Fazal and Abhimanyu Singh. Set around the Partition of India, the story examines the human cost of one of the most traumatic chapters in the subcontinent's history. Deol plays Sikander Mirza, while Zinta portrays Hamida Mirza and Azmi takes on the role of Mai. The narrative revolves around a Muslim family that moves into a house in Lahore after Partition, only to encounter the Hindu woman who remains connected to the property, bringing questions of displacement, identity, loss and humanity to the forefront. The movie also reunites Santoshi and Deol while bringing Deol and Zinta back together on screen, adding another layer of nostalgia. Interestingly, Shabana Azmi is the common link between the two Hindi releases, appearing in pivotal roles in both films. The two Bollywood releases, however, have another major challenge to contend with: Marvel's 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day', which has already been playing in Indian cinemas since July 30. Starring Tom Holland, Zendaya, Jacob Batalon, Jon Bernthal and Mark Ruffalo, the superhero movie has established a strong theatrical presence before the arrival of the two new Hindi films. With the Hollywood smash hit already commanding screens and audience attention, 'Awarapan 2' and 'Batwara 1947' will have to carve out their own space through their respective strengths – nostalgia and music on one side and star power, emotion and historical drama on the other. The Independence Day weekend therefore sets up an intriguing three-way box-office battle. Live Events 10:05 (IST) Aug 14 Batwara 1947 movie review: Strong word of mouth The initial reactions suggest that 'Batwara 1947' could benefit from positive word of mouth. The movie has received praise from viewers who watched morning shows.
Adding to this, The reported reactions indicate that Sunny Deol's performance remains one of the movie's biggest attractions. The movie's message of communal harmony has also been appreciated.
Meanwhile, Shabana Azmi is another key performer in the two-movie ticket-window conversation. She plays an important role in 'Batwara 1947' and has been lauded by early viewers.

Notably, The movie's emotional approach appears to have connected with audiences. Sunny Deol's character and the movie's focus on humanity have also emerged as recurring points in the early reactions.
As per the latest buzz, The story's central character continues to be Shivam Pandit. The reviewers lauded the writers for keeping his journey at the heart of the sequel.

In further updates, X review shared, "Writers #BilalSiddiqui and #VisheshBhatt ensure that the backbone of the story – #ShivamPandit – remains the focal point... The writers also know when to hold back and when to hit hard, resulting in several sequences that genuinely stay with you."
On top of that, The review also highlighted how the sequel uses moments from the first movie. These references are shared to strengthen the connection between the two films.

It added, "Additionally, he smartly incorporates flashes from the first part, leveraging the recall value and nostalgia factor... These moments seamlessly connect the two films while giving followers a sense of familiarity."

title: Shah Rukh Khan becomes Foxtale’s new brand ambassador; to represent serum, sunscreen and more
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The partnership marks a new phase for Foxtale, which was launched four years ago and has since built a consumer community of more than 10 million people. The brand positions itself around science-backed skincare formulated with Indian skin and climate in mind.

Adding to this, With ‘Let Your Glow Through’, Foxtale aims to expand its messaging beyond individual skincare products. According to the brand, its formulations are developed by focusing on the source of skin concerns rather than relying only on surface-level solutions.

Meanwhile, The philosophy also reflects the brand’s view that skincare should not be about constantly adding more products or trying to change one’s appearance. Instead, Foxtale believes skincare should help consumers care for and bring out what they already have.

Notably, The brand shared Shah Rukh Khan was chosen as its ambassador because his public image and career align with the values behind the new philosophy. Foxtale highlighted qualities such as confidence, authenticity and substance, which it believes have remained central to the star’s appeal over the years.

As per the latest buzz, Speaking about the announcement, Romita Mazumdar, Founder and CEO of Foxtale, shared, “Everything we've built at Foxtale has started with one belief: that lasting results come from understanding the source, not simply treating the surface. 'Let Your Glow Through' is an extension of that belief. And it will continue to be the philosophy that will guide everything going forward.”

In further updates, She added, “Shah Rukh Khan felt like a natural partner because he represents the same idea. Across decades, what people have connected with has never just been what they see, but who he is. We're delighted to have him join us as we take Foxtale into its next chapter.”

On top of that, Foxtale currently operates across skincare, body care, lip care and fragrance categories. The company says its products are developed using consumer insights and science, with a focus on the needs of Indian consumers.
With Khan joining the brand and the introduction of its new philosophy, Foxtale is looking to build its next phase around the idea of skincare that works “from the source, through the surface”.

title: Collective Studios' Historyverse announces original series on Bhagat Singh
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The series will move beyond the widely known chapters of Bhagat Singh's life to explore the person behind the icon; his childhood, formative experiences, intellectual influences and the social and political environment that shaped his worldview. It will trace the evolution of these experiences and ideas through the different chapters of his life, culminating in the revolutionary figure whose legacy continues to endure. Set against the backdrop of a changing India in the early 20th century, the story will examine how Bhagat Singh's ideas and convictions evolved to ultimately define his legacy.

Adding to this, For Manish Hathiramani, the project marks his debut as a producer and reflects a personal interest in exploring the lesser-known dimensions of India's history through historically rooted entertainment.

Meanwhile, Speaking about the project, Sudeep Lahiri, Head of Channels and Distribution at Collective Media Network, shared, “There are some figures in our history whose stories we think we know completely. Bhagat Singh is one of them. But behind the icon was a young man whose ideas, influences and experiences shaped the person he would become. That is the story we are interested in exploring. Having Manish come on board as a co-producer makes this collaboration particularly exciting, because we share a strong belief in finding new perspectives within stories that have already been told many times and bringing them to audiences with scale and ambition.”

Notably, Manish Hathiramani, Investor and Entrepreneur, shared, “Bhagat Singh is a figure whose life has always fascinated me, but what interests me most is the person before the legend. We know the revolutionary, the freedom fighter and the icon; this series gives us an opportunity to understand the many facets of Bhagat Singh's life and the journey that shaped him. I am delighted to be producing this project with Historyverse and to bring a fresh perspective on his life and legacy to audiences.”

As per the latest buzz, The series is currently in development, with its title, cast and further details to be revealed at a later date. The project joins Historyverse's expanding slate of Indian history and culturally rooted storytelling, which seeks to revisit significant figures, stories and traditions through contemporary formats and ambitious new approaches to storytelling.

title: Kangana Ranaut defends calling Naseeruddin Shah ‘lomdi’; says, “Whenever you look at his films, interviews or statements, it is always about Pakistan”
body: Here's the latest fashion moment turning heads:

Reiterating her position, Kangana as per reports told ANI, “I shared this about Naseeruddin Shah because he had made such a distasteful video in which he was making threats of this kind. And whenever you look at his films, interviews or statements, it is always about Pakistan. Yeh Pakistan ki prem katha kab khatam hogi? Jab dekho Pakistan ke prem mein yeh mare rahte hain. Ab Partition ko bhi itne saal ho gaye hain toh yeh love story khatam kyun nahi ho rahi hai (When will this love story with Pakistan end? They are always lost in love for Pakistan. It has been so many years since the Partition, when will they end this love story?)

Adding to this, The star turned politician also recalled the protests she experienced personally and claimed that demonstrators had gathered outside her residence. Describing the situation, she shared, “People even climbed up to the gate of my house; there were at least two and a half thousand people outside, and such a massive police force had to be deployed that we couldn't sleep at night.” She added, “So when a situation like this was unfolding at Jantar Mantar, they were all shedding crocodile tears.”

Meanwhile, Kangana further questioned Bollywood’s response to protests involving young people, drawing a comparison with the ongoing situation in Jharkhand. Taking aim at what she considers selective solidarity within the industry, she went on to say, “But now that children in Jharkhand are facing this kind of oppression, aren’t they Gen Z too? Is someone only considered Gen Z if they act against the country or abuse the Prime Minister? They themselves have been made to appear anti-youth. This hypocrisy in the movie industry will not work. The crocodile tears that people from the movie industry were shedding for Jantar Mantar, they should shed the same tears for the children in Jharkhand as well.”

Notably, Speaking about her earlier remark directed towards Naseeruddin Shah, Kangana had shared, “Sach toh yeh hai har koi kisi na kisi ka kutta hai, lekin mujhe iss baat ka garv hai ki main jis ghar (desh) ki roti khati hoon uski rakhwali karti hoon/uske liye ladti hoon, Nasir Saab khaate toh iss desh ka hain lekin ladte padose desh keliye hain. (The truth is, everyone is someone's dog; but I take pride in the fact that I guard--and fight for--the household (country) whose bread I eat. Nasir Saab, on the other hand, eats this country's bread but fights for the neighboring country).”

As per the latest buzz, She then addressed her use of the term “lomdi”, making it clear that she stood by the remark. Kangana shared, “PS In today's time it's a compliment for humans to be called a dog because loyalty and cuteness are so rare. I'd rather be a dog than a lomdi like Nasiruddin.”

In further updates, Kangana’s latest comments come as she continues to voice her opinions on political and social issues, while her remarks about Naseeruddin Shah remain part of the larger conversation around differing viewpoints within the Indian movie industry.

title: Aaradhya Bachchan case: Delhi High Court asks if Bachchan family reputation extends across generations
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani raised the issue during the hearing while discussing the legal protection attached to a person's reputation. The judge questioned whether the reputation associated with a prominent family name could be compared with the goodwill attached to a trademark and, if so, how far such protection could extend.

Adding to this, “The value of trademark and reputation in the trademark arises from the fact that a product or service has been rendered. Now, this is somewhat contextually different when you are talking about a person. A certain last name has a reputation because of the achievements, the eminence in a certain field of work, etc. So, does that reputation, you are couching it as virtually as a trademark, does that flow down generationally? If so, up to what point?” Justice Bhambhani remarked.

Meanwhile, The Court subsequently framed three broad questions that it will consider in the matter. It asked whether a family name, when associated with a reputation similar to that of a trademark, can retain that reputation across generations and, if so, to what extent.

Notably, The Court will also examine whether fake news, even when it is “of egregiously despicable nature”, can constitute an intellectual property rights violation and, if it does, what specific category of intellectual property rights may be involved.

As per the latest buzz, Another question concerns the relationship between defamation and intellectual property law. The Court will consider whether the legal concepts of slander, libel or other forms of injury to reputation can be treated as intellectual property rights.
In further updates, “These are the general questions in my mind. This is not exhaustive,” the Court clarified.

On top of that, Aaradhya Bachchan, through her father Abhishek Bachchan, approached the Delhi High Court in 2023 against several YouTube channels and unidentified individuals, commonly referred to as John Doe defendants. The suit sought to prevent the publication of content that allegedly tarnished the Bachchan family name, invaded their privacy or made defamatory claims about Aaradhya.

The case specifically referred to multiple YouTube videos that made false claims about Aaradhya’s health. Some videos allegedly claimed that she was seriously unwell and had been admitted to a hospital, while another claimed that the minor had died. The content also allegedly accused her family of failing to provide her with timely medical treatment.

title: EXCLUSIVE: V. Shantaram biopic starring Siddhant Chaturvedi and Tamannaah Bhatia pushed to 2027; director reveals reason for delay
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Speaking exclusively to Bollywood Hungama , the movie's director, Abhijeet Shirish Deshpande, has clarified that the V. Shantaram biopic is very much on track and production has instead been moved to 2027. “We had initially planned an April shoot and planned to go indoors after rains. But we were delayed by two months, and then the whole schedule went haywire. Now with the fresh dates, we are planning to shoot next year with a few more big names in the casting apart from Sidharth and Tamannaah,” the filmmaker revealed.

Adding to this, The makers are now aiming to commence its shooting in April 2027. The revised schedule has been planned in a way that will allow the team to complete outdoor sequences first and then utilize the monsoon period for interior shoots.

Meanwhile, The movie chronicles Shantaram’s remarkable journey from the silent era through the advent of sound and color, showcasing his evolution as one of India’s most influential filmmakers. Shantaram is known for directing memorable films in Hindi and Marathi, including Do Aankhen Barah Haath (1957), Dr. Kotnis Ki Amar Kahani (1946), Amar Bhoopali (1951), and Pinjara (1971).

Notably, The project marks Siddhant Chaturvedi's first biographical role, and he's excited to get into the skin of the visionary filmmaker known for his signature style of lavish sets, unique song picturizations, and visual symbolism. During the announcement, he had called the opportunity one of the greatest honors of his life. “The more I read about his journey, the more humbled I felt. He wasn’t just a pioneer of Indian and global cinema, he was a visionary who kept pushing forward no matter the obstacles,” Chaturvedi shared. “Stepping into his world has been my most transformative experience as an star. His life moved me deeply and reminded me of the power of perseverance. It’s a lesson I hope to hold close, both in my work and in every moment of my life.”

title: Shilpa Shetty, Arjun Kapoor to join Kiran Bedi, Jai Madaan and others at World Happpiness Summit 2026 in Bengaluru
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The summit will be held at New Horizon College of Engineering against the backdrop of Bengaluru, a city known for technology, innovation, entrepreneurship and professional ambition. The conversations will look at happiness beyond achievements, financial milestones and social status, with sessions around purpose, relationships, inner peace, mental well-being, fulfilment and the pressures that accompany modern success. Shilpa Shetty and Arjun Kapoor will bring perspectives from entertainment and popular culture, while Kiran Bedi, Sonu Sharma, Hema Sardesai, Jai Madaan and Dr. Saamdu Chetri will contribute perspectives from public service, entrepreneurship, music, wellness, spirituality and the philosophy of Gross National Happiness.

Adding to this, At the centre of the summit is Happpy AiR - Atman in Ravi’s belief that true ‘Happpiness’ is a harmonious mix of Pleasure, Peace and Purpose — the three Ps. “We spend so much of our lives preparing to become happpy someday, after the next achievement, the next milestone or the next success. But happiness is not a destination we arrive at. It is something we can experience in the present moment,” he shared. He added that the three Ps form the basis of his understanding of happiness (that’s the reason why he spells happpiness with three Ps) and that the summit is an effort to take this thought beyond an individual philosophy and create a larger conversation around what it means to live a happy and fulfilled life.

Meanwhile, The World Happpiness Summit is part of the larger #Happpy.AiR.Movement, which seeks to create a wider dialogue around happiness, inner peace and purposeful living. The initiative comes at a time when Bengaluru continues to attract entrepreneurs, technology professionals, creators and young talent from across India, and seeks to explore whether a city known for ambition and opportunity can also become a benchmark for happiness and well-being. The World Happpiness Summit 2026 will be held on September 24 at New Horizon College of Engineering, Bengaluru.

title: Awarapan 2 beats part 1's lifetime box office haul with advance bookings alone, Emraan Hashmi film set for massive start
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

It may come as a surprise to many younger readers who keep hearing only positive things about Emraan Hashmi ’s Awarapan from older audiences, but when it rolled out in 2007, the movie was a ticket-window bomb. The ambitious movie from Vishesh Films managed to earn a mere ₹ 7.7 crore rupees net in its lifetime. But over the years, as viewers discovered it on home media, cable, and eventually streaming, Awarapan gained a cult following. That belated credibility and love are now helping the sequel, set to rollout this weekend. Awarapan 2 is tracking to have one of the biggest openings for Bollywood in 2026. In fact, the buzz is so strong that the movie is set to cross part 1’s lifetime earnings even before rollout.

Adding to this, Emraan Hashmi on the promotional poster of Awarapan 2.
